title: Senior Program Manager, 3P Seafood Distribution, Whole Foods Market
descriptionHtml:
Whole Foods Market (WFM) sources seafood through a complex network of third-party distributors whose performance directly determines what customers find on the shelf. This role owns that network, from the contracts that govern it, the relationships that sustain it, and the strategic path forward for how WFM partners with 3Ps to meet quality, availability, and cost-to-serve goals at scale. You will be the single-threaded owner for 3P seafood distributor contract management and performance and the strategic architect helping WFM define what the right 3P model looks like going forward. This means owning both the operational rigor (contract terms, service levels, compliance) and the longer-horizon strategic thinking, challenging assumptions about how WFM's seafood distribution network should be structured to protect quality differentiation and supply security over the long-term.

This is a high-visibility, high-complexity role that sits at the intersection of Procurement, Inventory Planning, Store Operations, Finance, and Supplier Partnerships. The right candidate brings deep distributor contract experience, strong financial modeling skills, and the credibility to lead WFM's 3P strategy in a perishable’s environment where margin, quality, and supply continuity are non-negotiable.


Key job responsibilities
3P Seafood Distributor Contract Management & Negotiations
•Own the full lifecycle of 3P seafood distributor contracts: from initial scoping, RFP/RFQ, and negotiation through execution, renewal, amendment, and termination. This includes fee structures, service-level agreements, delivery schedules, quality standards, cold-chain requirements, and cost-to-serve terms.
•Lead negotiations on rate increases, new service charges, and contract amendments: building and defending WFM's counter-position with documented cost offsets, volume commitments, and business case modeling. When distributors issue unilateral rate changes, own the response framework and resolution.
•Develop and maintain a contract management framework: renewal timelines, escalation triggers, performance benchmarks, and obligation tracking across all active 3P seafood distributor relationships. Maintain centralized repository of key terms, expiration dates, and open obligations.
•Monitor distributor performance against contractual obligations: fill rates, on-time delivery, EDI compliance (including ASN accuracy), cold-chain integrity, and spec adherence. Quantify gaps, drive resolution, and escalate when underperformance creates store-level or financial risk.
•Partner with Finance to model contract economics: total cost of distribution, landed cost impact by distributor, and financial exposure from service failures or contract changes. Build business cases for contract restructuring, consolidation, or termination decisions.

3P Strategy & Path Forward for WFM
•Lead the development of WFM's 3P seafood distributor strategy: defining what the right distributor model looks like across a 2–3 year horizon. This includes evaluating distributor consolidation opportunities, exclusivity arrangements, delivery frequency optimization, co-investment structures, and how 3P relationships ladder up to WFM's quality, supply security, and cost-to-serve goals.
•Assess current 3P distributor network against WFM's regional supply requirements: identify coverage gaps, redundancies, cost-to-serve inefficiencies, and capability constraints (e.g., cold-chain infrastructure, processing capacity, delivery frequency). Translate findings into actionable network design recommendations.
•Design and manage distributor onboarding and qualification frameworks: defining the standards (quality, compliance, EDI, cold-chain, financial stability) new 3P partners must meet before going live. Own the go-live process for new distributor relationships including cross-functional readiness (Procurement, IP, Store Ops, Finance).
•Identify and evaluate opportunities for strategic 3P partnerships: including exclusivity arrangements, co-investment in processing or logistics capacity, and multi-year supply commitments that create competitive advantage for WFM. Build and present business cases to leadership for partnership structures that go beyond transactional distribution agreements.
•Serve as WFM's primary point of escalation and resolution when distributor relationships reach inflection points: contract disputes, service failures, unilateral cost actions, or capacity constraints that threaten store-level availability. Own the resolution playbook and the outcome.

Distributor Performance Management & Compliance
•Build and own the 3P distributor scorecard: tracking performance across fill rate, on-time delivery, EDI/ASN compliance, invoice accuracy, spec adherence, and cold-chain integrity. Use scorecard data to drive accountability conversations, renegotiations, and network-level decisions.
•Own the delivery schedule coordination process between 3P distributors and WFM DCs: ensuring schedule changes are communicated cross-functionally to Procurement, Inventory Planning, and Store Operations before store-facing communications go out. Prevent coordination failures that create downstream supply risk.
•Manage distributor compliance with WFM quality standards, animal welfare certifications, and labeling/documentation requirements. Escalate spec violations with financial impact quantification and a defined remediation timeline. Ensure compliance failures are resolved — not absorbed silently.

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Management
•Serve as the connective tissue between 3P distributors and WFM's internal functions of Procurement, Inventory Planning, Store Operations, Finance, and Legal. Ensure distributor commitments are operationally real and that internal teams have what they need to execute against them.
•Lead cross-functional working sessions to resolve distributor-related conflicts, align on go-live readiness, and unblock execution. Develop and deliver executive-level communications on distributor contract status, negotiation outcomes, strategic recommendations, and path-forward options.
•Manage competing priorities across DC Operations, Finance, and Supplier teams to maintain program momentum on distributor transitions, new go-lives, and contract renegotiations. Document program outcomes, lessons learned, and playbooks for future distributor management.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Knowledge of general AI tools
- Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions

descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

We are looking for a highly skilled Senior Thermal Design Engineer who brings a strong blend of technical depth, research capability, and analytical rigor. The ideal candidate has a demonstrated history of delivering high-quality results on time and with efficiency.

-Perform Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to evaluate and optimize thermal performance across product designs
-Develop and refine thermal design processes, methodologies, and best practices to drive continuous improvement
-Design, build, and validate thermal hardware prototypes to support product development milestones
-Deliver rapid thermal design input, trade-off analyses, and actionable recommendations to hardware architects and cross-functional teams

Amazon LEO’s Thermal Team is responsible for the thermal design solutions for all components in Kuiper’s satellites and customer terminals. They work together with many engineering disciplines (e.g., mechanical, power, electrical, network) to find the design that maximizes performance while minimizing mass, cost and manufacturing complexity, and enabling all components to operate reliably over the satellite’s target lifetime. The team follows all hardware components from conceptual design, detailed analysis, development testing, through launch and flight.

Preferred qualifications

title: Sr. Broadband Phased Array Antenna Architect, Payload Architecture Team
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite constellation initiative designed to bring fast, affordable broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. We are building a next-generation satellite system from the ground up — designing everything from the spacecraft and payload to the ground infrastructure and customer terminals. This is a rare opportunity to join a team that is shaping the future of global connectivity at scale.

We are looking for a Broadband Phased Array Architect to join the Payload Architecture team in San Diego. You will be a key technical contributor to the architecture of our broadband satellite payload — a Ka-band multi-beam phased array system that delivers high-throughput connectivity to proprietary customer terminals on the ground. You will work alongside experienced architects and engineers, helping shape the broadband phased array architecture as it evolves through current and future satellite generations.

This role uniquely spans both RF and digital domains. You will need depth in digital beamforming architectures including FPGA and ASIC platforms, high-speed serial interconnects, beamforming algorithm implementation, and capacity mode management. You will also need Ka-band RF front-end experience and understanding of multi-beam satellite link design.

You will define phased array requirements and work with the verification team to validate them through test. You will collaborate with systems, HW design, silicon, antenna, modem, calibration, thermal, power, mechanical, reliability, communication systems, regulatory, and verification teams to ensure architecture and requirements are achievable.

Beyond the current payload, you will evaluate emerging technologies and contribute to the architecture roadmap for future satellite generations — including new digital beamforming approaches, advanced interconnects, and next-generation semiconductor processes. This is a hands-on role — you will be in the lab, in the data, and on call when satellites are live. If you have experience with multi-beam satellite payloads or Ka-band phased arrays, we want to hear from you.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
● Translate high-level throughput and coverage requirements into broadband payload requirements — accounting for thermal, power, mechanical, reliability, and mass constraints
● Propose and own the broadband phased array architecture spanning the full signal chain from Ka-band antenna element through RF front-end through digital beamforming backbone to modem interface
● Work with systems, HW design, antenna, silicon, and calibration teams to realize the architecture
● Contribute to customer link performance — working with systems and customer terminal teams to meet end-to-end link requirements
● Define phased array requirements that flow from system-level needs down to subsystem and component specifications
● Work with the verification team to develop test plans that validate those requirements
● Define signal integrity requirements for high-speed serial links based on SerDes technology selection, and review analysis performed by the SI team
● Support Ka-band RF front-end architecture trade studies across multiple semiconductor process technologies
● Drive capacity mode management architecture — how the payload scales beams and reconfigures resources based on demand
● Evaluate emerging technologies to inform the next generation architecture roadmap
● Support production and on-orbit debug — this role is hands-on and on-call

A day in the life
You split your time between the current program and next generation. On any given day you might translate throughput requirements into payload requirements, review beamforming simulations, define signal integrity requirements for serial links, run capacity mode trade studies, or refine requirements based on verification testability. You contribute to customer link analysis and work across HW design, antenna, silicon, and calibration teams to realize the architecture. Some weeks you evaluate new digital beamforming approaches and define the architecture roadmap for future satellites. Other days you are in the lab checking results or supporting production debug.

About the team
The Payload Architecture team is part of the Antenna organization at Amazon Leo. We are a small group of senior architects responsible for the phased array architecture across Amazon Leo’s satellite programs. We define the architecture, drive requirements, run trade studies, and make sure everything works from prototype through orbit. Our scope extends to customer link performance — working with systems and customer terminal teams to close end-to-end link budgets. We work closely with every engineering team on the payload and pride ourselves on being hands-on problem solvers. We are based in San Diego.

Basic qualifications

- Master's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering/Communications Engineering, or experience with modern ASIC/FPGA design and verification tools
- Experience in developing link and system level simulators using MATLAB, Python, or C++
- Experience with RF measurement equipment, including: power meters, spectrum analyzers, vector signal generators, network analyzers, oscilloscopes
- Experience in wireless system design and architecture, system integration, and RF system analysis
- Experience with analog, digital, and high-speed circuit design
- 7+ years of experience in Ka-band RF system design, multi-beam satellite payload architecture, or digital phased array design relying on high speed serdes interconnects

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in Space Vehicle/Satellite Operations, Space Communications or related industry
- PhD in electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics or physics
- Experience participating in or leading technical collaborations and creating alignment across diverse groups (e.g., hardware engineering, software engineering, program management)
- Experience with multi-beam satellite payload capacity mode management or resource allocation
- Experience with Ka-band or mm-wave RF front-end design across multiple semiconductor process technologies
- Familiarity with phased array calibration, synchronization and over-the-air test methodology

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Advertising operates at the intersection of eCommerce and advertising, offering a rich array of digital advertising solutions with the goal of helping consumers find and discover products and services. We help advertisers reach global audiences via Amazon owned and operated sites (Amazon.com, IMDb.com), millions of Fire TVs, Kindles, and Fire Tablets, and on high-quality sites across the internet via the Amazon DSP.  With a range of flexible pricing and buying models, our advertising solutions help businesses build brand awareness, increase product sales, and solidify brand loyalty.  If you are interested in joining a world-class advertising group with a relentless focus on the customer, you’ve come to the right place.

Amazon Adapt is a program designed to offer coverage solutions for business gaps which may occur due to extended leave (parental, medical) and unexpected account transitions.  Amazon Adapt deploys highly skilled, hyper-agile talent that ensures customers can continue to invest in their partnerships with Amazon Advertising, uninterrupted. The program ensures that the high bar for customer service, strategic partnership, and revenue attainment is maintained during these coverage gaps.

As a member of the Amazon Adapt team, you will have the opportunity to complete a series of rotations across a range of consumer industries.  This enables Adapt team members to experience high-velocity exposure to teams across the organization and to clients across different verticals.  From day 1 Adapt team members must use their experience to earn trust with multiple stakeholders and take ownership of account relationships within a team.  As a member of the Adapt team you will use your experience and vast knowledge to drive results for advertisers and internal stakeholders. Adapt team members are decisive, knowledgeable, and use high judgement. The Adapt role will give you a chance to Learn and be Curious and the autonomy to own projects that will help you advance your career at Amazon. The Adapt team prioritizes flexibility, and hires for both 40 and 30 hour work weeks.

As a Full Funnel Seller on the Adapt team, you will serve as the sole commercial point of contact for advertiser accounts during leave of absence coverage periods. You will independently own all client relationships, revenue targets, and product selling. For endemic accounts, you will manage the full product suite across SPB, Display, and Video. For non-endemic accounts, you will manage DSP renewals, audience strategy, and multi-tactic adoption across Performance+, Brand+, and 3P Deals. You will execute sprint-based playbook-driven pitches, manage DAA renewals, own the Salesforce pipeline end-to-end, and maintain 100% pitch coverage and zero dark periods across a book of 4 accounts.

If you are ready to make an immediate impact, embrace change, and accelerate your career at Amazon, come join us!

Key job responsibilities
- Independently own all client relationships and revenue for a book of business
- Execute sprint-based playbook-driven pitches across the full product suite
- Manage full-funnel selling: SPB + Display + Video (endemic) or DSP + P+ + B+ + 3P Deals (non-endemic)
- Own Salesforce pipeline end-to-end including DAA renewals and forecasting
- Deliver 100% pitch coverage and 90%+ renewal rates
- Maintain zero dark periods greater than 60 days
- Conduct quarterly sprint themes from Core4 diagnostic (endemic) or quarterly performance reviews (non-endemic)
- Present QBRs, campaign performance reviews, and proposals to clients
- Identify and execute upsell/cross-sell opportunities across the full product suite
- Manage all sales calls, proposals, and stakeholder relationships independently
- Collaborate with partner teams via scaled support model (office hours, pitch repository)
- This is a client-facing role and requires up to 20% domestic travel as needed

A day in the life
As a Full Funnel Seller on the Adapt team, you start your day with a pipeline review in Salesforce, checking renewal timelines, campaign pacing, and upcoming pitch deadlines across your accounts. You then lead a client call to discuss campaign performance, present optimization recommendations, and advance a Video pitch (endemic) or DSP audience refresh (non-endemic). Mid-morning, you prepare a sprint pitch using playbook templates for an upcoming quarterly presentation. After lunch, you conduct a campaign optimization review, identify upsell opportunities, and draft a proposal. You close out the day updating Salesforce, managing stakeholder follow-ups, and planning tomorrow's client meetings. You own the entire commercial relationship for your accounts.

About the team
The Amazon Adapt team specializes in dynamic work. Our team supports the Global Amazon Ads Organization during gaps in business coverage due to leaves of absence, roles to be hired, and unexpected employee movement. Amazon Adapt's vision is to provide the world's most customer-centric business coverage, exceeding both customer and employee expectations during periods of transition.

This role provides rotational coverage for single-seller accounts where you own the advertiser relationship. When a single seller goes on LOA or there is a TBH, Adapt is the only solution to maintain account relationships and protect revenue. You will operate as the sole point of contact across the full product suite. The Adapt team prioritizes flexibility and hires for both 40 and 30 hour work weeks.

- Experience closing sales and generating revenue
- Experience driving demand and managing a customer funnel across multiple channels
- Experience with CRM tools like Salesforce
- Experience with communication, presentation, and negotiation
- Experience reviewing and analyzing performance metrics to identify areas of opportunity that will drive performance improvement
- 4+ years of experience in digital advertising with independent selling experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in e-commerce, retail or advertising

- Experience in audience segmentation and targeting

title: Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, AWS Billing
descriptionHtml:
We're rebuilding the AWS product catalog for an AI-native world, and this role owns both how it's defined and how it grows. You'll set the standards every AWS product follows and define the new features, packages, and add-ons that service teams bring to customers, building the machine-readable foundation that billing, cost management, and AI agents all depend on. The AWS Billing organization serves over 200 AWS services across 30+ regions, and every one needs a product definition that is structurally correct, consistently described, and rich enough for both humans and AI to reason about. This is the foundation for commercial decisions made by external customers and internal teams.

As Senior Product Manager - Technical External Services, you'll own the AWS product model end to end: the schema, governance rules, and quality standards every product conforms to, and the new product structures service teams build on top of them. You'll define what attributes a product carries from creation, how to create standard models for different types of services (from compute and storage to AI inference and developer tools), how products relate to and compose with one another in packages and shared commercial experiences, and how the catalog enables AI agents to discover, compare, and act on products programmatically. You'll also extend the catalog with new product features, packages, and add-ons that service teams can adopt through configuration rather than custom engineering. Your work directly determines how AWS services launch and grow their products.

In this role, you'll architect the data model that underlies AWS commerce, define the governance framework that enforces it across hundreds of service teams, and establish the lifecycle and relationship standards that let products evolve and work consistently across commercial channels. You'll conduct direct research with service teams and internal consumers of product data to understand where definitions break down, translating those insights into schema improvements and governance rules. You'll work at the intersection of data architecture, billing infrastructure, and AI-native product design, defining how AWS products present themselves to the next generation of consumers.

You'll collaborate with engineering teams across AWS's billing, metering, and cost management organizations. This role requires deep technical fluency in data modeling, schema design, and systems thinking, combined with the product instinct to know which standards matter and which create bureaucracy.

If you're excited about defining the foundational data layer that makes AWS's commerce systems work this role offers the chance to shape how every AWS product is defined, described, and used across AWS commerce.

Key job responsibilities
- Define product framework: schema, required attributes, quality rules, and lifecycle governance for every AWS product
- Define standard product models and product-relationship patterns for different service categories
- Extend the catalog with new product features, packages, and add-ons that service teams can adopt through configuration
- Architect agent-readable product metadata standards for AI consumption across internal and external experiences
- Drive adoption of product standards across new offerings and established catalog systems
- Conduct direct research with service teams and product data consumers to identify where definitions break down and drive improvements
- Partner with engineering teams across AWS's billing, metering, and cost management organizations

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of working as a Technical Product Manager experience
- Experience working with customers, technical teams, and management to collect requirements, describe software product features, and technical designs
- Experience in taking a product from conception & definition phase through engineering design and taking it to market
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, finance, or economics

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience working within teams delivering software products and features using agile methodologies
- 3+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using data modeling experience
- Experience developing, deploying and managing AI products at scale
- Experience with billing, commerce, or catalog systems
- Experience building or designing agentic products and interfaces

title: Associate Corporate Counsel, Amazon Ads Legal
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, our legal professionals play a critical role in enabling business teams to innovate while managing risk effectively. As an Amazon Ads Legal Associate Corporate Counsel, you will advise on a range of legal matters, conduct product counseling, draft and negotiate contracts, and provide practical guidance that helps teams move quickly and confidently. You will work across functions to deliver clear, actionable legal advice on issues that matter — from commercial agreements to regulatory compliance. If you are a collaborative, curious attorney who enjoys translating legal complexity into straightforward recommendations, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at scale.

In this role, you will be the principal legal support for IMDb, including IMDb's contracts, ad services, customer experiences, licensing, compliance, and much more. You will work directly with senior business leaders, providing guidance across an array of issues. In addition to supporting IMDb, this role also includes providing guidance and thought leadership on emerging AI initiatives that cut across Amazon businesses.

Key job responsibilities
- Assess Amazon Ads product and service proposals against regulatory requirements, AI transparency obligations, privacy promises, and other legal considerations.
- Learn the ins, outs, nuts, and bolts of how your clients' products and services work at a technical level to enable you to provide surgically precise legal advice.
- Provide clear, practical legal advice to internal stakeholders by researching and interpreting applicable statutes, regulations, and case law to support sound decision-making.
- Identify and assess legal risks across projects and programs, recommending mitigation strategies and escalating issues when appropriate.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize legal processes, develop best practices, and create templates or playbooks that improve efficiency and consistency.
- Draft, review, and negotiate a variety of commercial contracts and agreements, ensuring terms appropriately protect the organization while enabling business objectives.
- Prepare and organize legal documentation to comply with professional standards and guidelines, and support program management efforts by tracking progress and communicating priorities to stakeholders.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a contract proposal, working through key terms and preparing a summary of your recommendations. After a quick call with business stakeholders, you shift to researching a regulatory question that surfaced the previous day. In the afternoon, you join a cross-functional working session to help refine a new process for handling a recurring legal issue. Then, you switch back to writing a document describing how Amazon will manage legal risks, customer trust considerations, and commercial strategic data leakage issues associated with a new product proposal. title: Associate Corporate Counsel, Amazon Ads
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a product or tech lawyer to join the Amazon Legal team supporting Amazon Ads.

Amazon Ads helps advertisers reach customers across Amazon properties (e.g., Amazon.com, IMDb TV, Twitch, Fire TV, and Amazon Music) and tens of thousands of third-party (3P) websites and apps. As Associate Corporate Counsel, you will counsel Advertising Trust team on policy and product development questions and ad tech issues at a time when AI is fundamentally reshaping the advertising landscape. AI-powered creative tools now allow brands to generate product-in-use videos and lifestyle imagery that previously required full production shoots, while AI-powered optimization is making full-funnel advertising simpler and more accessible. Agentic AI is also entering the commerce layer, with AI assistants beginning to influence purchasing decisions and platforms integrating paid advertising into conversational shopping experiences. These developments create novel legal questions across the ad tech stack. You will handle legal issues in business-centric ways and develop processes that address risk while allowing the business flexibility and freedom to quickly develop services that prioritize and delight our customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Counseling product and engineering teams on the development and deployment of AI-driven advertising features
- Advising on emerging regulatory and compliance requirements for AI in advertising
- Navigating the intersection of programmatic advertising and agentic AI

- Advising on data governance for AI-powered advertising products, including audience data use and cross-platform measurement in an evolving privacy landscape
- Partnering with privacy, policy, trust and safety, and engineering teams to build scalable legal frameworks that keep pace with rapid product innovation

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a policy review as the Advertising Trust team evaluates how a new AI powered ad moderation tool can be used to enable or disable advertising for certain products or services or in certain locales. By midday you could be advising sales teams on onboarding a new brand advertising highly regulated services to customers. Later in the afternoon you might work with policy managers to develop a scalable ad content policy risk framework to cover new advertising placements that complies with consumer protection laws and privacy laws worldwide. The common thread across every conversation is the same: finding business centric ways to address legal risk while giving the team the flexibility to build quickly and keep customers at the center.

Do you enjoy watching the latest movies, television shows, or sporting events on your computer, tablet or smartphone? Do you hate waiting for your pages to load or your show to re-buffer? Do you want to contribute to systems that deliver a flawless experience in serving video from the edge? Good - us too.

AWS Cloudfront is looking for experienced Software Development Engineer to join our team and lead critical initiatives!

At AWS Cloudfront, working on systems with global scale is a daily part of the job. We solve hard problems. We build reliable, scalable, low-cost systems that serve our ever-growing customer base. We are constantly shipping features that drive innovation in the CDN market. We deliver an elegant geo-distributed platform to serve not only video from the edge, but a wide variety of use cases.

We:
- Are a fast-growing, agile and collaborative group of technologists from diverse backgrounds
- Are inventors and owners, building new technologies and improving existing ones
- Obsess over our customer’s needs and experience
- Enjoy the prototyping and tinkering stages, as well as the rigor of making solutions production-ready

If you:
- Enjoy seeing the impact your work has on real customers
- Are comfortable in an agile environment and understand the importance of working/developing iteratively
- Value being a part of a strong team of technologists and collaborating with them to build BIG things
- Take ownership and show determination to get the job done
- Want to create services at a massive scale used by millions of people
- Are naturally curious about how systems operate at scale and think of ways to constantly improve those systems
- Learn from others and help grow those in your team to achieve their best
...then this is the role for you!


Key job responsibilities
- Design for new systems from scratch or improving existing systems and own the technical direction for the initiative from start to finish.

- Play the technical advisor role by mentoring and guiding the team members to solve complex problems with simple solutions.

- Drive the big ideas to improve availability and performance initiatives across the organizations.

- Involve in both coding and code reviews.

About the team
Our team's charter is:

We build and manage the components like CloudFront Core Routing, Anycast Routing, L4LB, Traffic Director, DNS and Backbone Intelligent Routing.

The services are built using variety of technologies like Rust, C/C++, Java, eBPF XDP, Kinesis, Lambda, DynamoDB, ElasticCache etc.

Experience in one or more of these technologies along with real world practices on the software engineering principles and fundamentals are ideal for this role.

The candidate will have the opportunity to work on one or more services that handled the traffic for the events like Cricket World Cup, FIFA World Cup, Thursday Night Football etc.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Senior Technical Program Manager - S3 Storage, S3 Keystone
descriptionHtml:
Are you excited about the incredible opportunity that cloud computing represents? Are you passionate about delivering high quality services and ready to apply your experience at massive scale?

Amazon Web Services' Cloud Storage, AWS S3, is one of the largest distributed storage systems in the world. Managing trillions of objects in storage, retrieving them in sub-x ms, building software that deploys to tens of thousands of hosts, achieving 99.999999999% durability. These are just a few of the numbers that give you a sense of the scale of the exciting problems you will find every day working in Simple Storage Service (S3). Amazon S3 powers businesses across the globe that make the lives of consumers better daily. Whether its electronic content delivered to your home, technology that betters your remote working experience, allows you to plan travel to exotic places or simply get stuff delivered to your home. As a TPM in S3, you get to deliver these capabilities and delight our customers working with teams of talented engineers and leaders.

S3 is looking for an talented and experienced TPM to drive forecast planning, capital cost management and utilization of S3 storage bytes. With Exabytes of storage under operation globally and growing, forecasting growth and managing the storage efficiently has a direct impact the bottom line for S3. You will partner with Engineering teams to define roadmap to manage the forecasting to stay ahead of customer demand and Capital planning for multi-million dollars efficiently. You will be responsible for defining how the roadmap is delivered, bringing teams across organizations together, anticipating bottlenecks, providing escalation management, driving necessary trade-offs by balancing the business needs and technical or resource constraints. An ability to take large, technically complex projects and break them down into manageable pieces, develop actionable plans and successfully deliver them is expected.

Utility Computing (UC)
AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS, including support for customers who require specialized security solutions for customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.

About AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon diversity conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience with server, storage, networking, or large-scale distributed systems

Preferred qualifications

title: Solutions Architect II, Amazon Web Services, Higher Education and State and Local Government
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about helping State and Local Government and Higher Education institutions unlock the transformative power of cloud technology? Amazon Web Services is seeking a Solutions Architect to serve as a trusted technical advisor to customers across the New England region. In this role, you'll combine your communication skills, problem-solving abilities, and eagerness to learn new technologies to guide diverse organizations through their cloud journey.

This is more than a typical technology consulting role. You'll work at the intersection of innovation and public service, helping government agencies and universities architect solutions that modernize their operations, improve citizen and student experiences, and achieve mission-critical outcomes. Your ability to understand complex technical challenges and translate them into actionable solutions will help grow our State and Local Government and Higher Education businesses while making a meaningful impact on communities across the region.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver cloud architecture solutions that meet infrastructure and application requirements for State and Local Government and Higher Education customers, incorporating best practices for security, scalability, and performance
- Lead architecture reviews, technical workshops, and proof-of-concept projects that demonstrate innovative cloud solutions and help customers envision transformative possibilities for their organizations
- Serve as a trusted technical advisor by taking the time to understand each customer's unique business context, technology challenges, and long-term goals, then translating those needs into technical requirements
- Collaborate with account teams, professional services, and AWS engineering groups to scope customer engagements with clear objectives, drive timely delivery of value, and ensure customer success throughout their cloud adoption journey
- Educate customers and internal teams by developing and delivering technical content such as presentations, workshops, and best practice guidance, while capturing and sharing knowledge that advances the broader Solutions Architecture community

A day in the life
Your day might begin with an architecture review session with a state agency exploring modernization options, followed by leading a hands-on workshop that demonstrates serverless computing for a university IT team. After collaborating with your account team to develop a migration strategy, you'll build a proof-of-concept that illustrates the art of the possible with analytics and AI/ML services. You'll wrap up by joining a strategic planning discussion with a higher education CIO about how cloud technology can drive their institution's digital transformation objectives.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- 2+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 4+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working within software development or Internet-related industries
- Experience migrating or transforming legacy customer solutions to the cloud
- Experience working with AWS technologies from a dev/ops perspective

title: Senior Product Lifecycle Mechanical Engineer, Data Center Mechanical Products & Services
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer to be part of a global engineering team responsible for ownership and continuous improvement related to data center liquid cooling infrastructure products within our rapidly expanding data center footprint. We seek engineers with hands-on mechanical and manufacturing experience in liquid cooling products. Experience leading cooling product design, understanding cooling principles, and knowledge of quality manufacturing practices is essential. You should comprehend detailed equipment specifications, piping systems, pumping systems, air handler systems and evaluate design change implications.

As a Global Amazon Product Lifecycle Engineer, you'll support AWS data centers' liquid cooling infrastructure. You'll work with product development teams to understand products during development and testing, maintaining engineering ownership throughout operational life. You'll serve as the global engineering resource for liquid cooling AWS infrastructure in data centers.

Amazon has a global presence. Intermittent travel will be necessary and should be expected to be around 30%. Some travel will be domestic, but international travel will be necessary.


Key job responsibilities
• Possess strong engineering judgement and are able to provide recommendations despite uncertainty
• Are detail and data oriented
• Have experience engineering air handling, piping and/or pumping products
• Review, update, and approve equipment submittals
• Work with global liquid cooling equipment suppliers and manufacturers
• Build trust and relationships with different stakeholders (e.g. reliability, operations, design, compliance)
• Work on concurrent projects, in multiple geographic zones
• Understand and explain complex systems in clear and concise language
• Support Operations including failure mode and root cause analysis, maintenance and troubleshooting support, and operating procedure review for both mechanical and electrical issues.
• Listen to the voice of the customer to understand if there are improvements that can be made to increase product reliability or availability.
• Work with global supplier and manufacturers to design product improvements, and to oversee root cause analysis.
• Contribute to our global body of knowledge and drive a cycle of continuous improvement at a global scale

title: Instock Manager, Amazon Pharmacy
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon Pharmacy's Supply Chain team and help shape how medications reach patients. Amazon Pharmacy is looking for an experienced Instock Manager with proven experience managing complex inbound supply chains in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment. You will join a high-powered, collaborative team where you partner across multiple functions to keep patients supplied with the medications they depend on.

Pharmacy is one of the most meaningful and interesting supply chains you can work on. Every in-stock decision you make helps ensure a patient gets the medication they're counting on, so your work has a direct, tangible impact on people's health. It's also a rich problem space: you'll navigate product expiry, controlled-substance handling, and state-by-state regulations, solving challenges that don't exist in traditional retail. If you want the ownership of an instock role plus a mission that matters, this is a rare place to build.

The Instock Manager will be responsible for all aspects of the Instock role, including driving improved in-stock, inventory planning, and vendor operational improvement (efficiency, fill rates, lead times). You will drive initiatives to improve patient experience, reduce cost, and improve inventory health by working collaboratively across pharmacy operations, supply chain, procurement, and compliance teams. The ideal candidate excels in scalable process improvement, automation, and analytics, and is energized by solving complex problems and turning manual processes into scalable ones.

Strong written and verbal communication skills are required, and the candidate should be comfortable engaging with both internal stakeholders and vendors. The candidate will have proven experience delivering results by partnering with others and be comfortable contributing across a range of topics outside the core ISM responsibilities.

Key job responsibilities
Maintain excellent in-stock rates for owned category and/or region while minimizing expiry and unhealthy inventory
Execute inventory strategies to optimize service levels, turns, and inventory health under expiry and controlled-substance constraints
Monitor, analyze, and own key performance indicators such as in-stock rate, target inventory levels, fill rate, turns, and expiry/write-off rates
Manage efficient inbound and outbound inventory flows and health, including supporting purchasing processes and removing unproductive or expiring inventory in a compliant manner
Drive root cause analysis and reporting on operational issues, develop action plans, and project manage improvements while managing multiple competing priorities simultaneously
Partner with vendor managers to drive vendor performance across fill rate, lead time, and reliability
Work collaboratively with internal teams to drive tools and process improvements affecting purchasing and procurement workflows, with emphasis on automating tasks currently performed manually
Ensure inventory and procurement decisions adhere to pharmacy regulatory and compliance requirements across states

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of supply chain, inventory management or project management experience
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience using strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills
- Experience with SQL and advanced Excel
- Ability to thrive in a high energy environment where tactical and strategic activities are expected to be driven in parallel

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field
- Track record of delivering results and an ability to operate both strategically and tactically in a high-energy, fast-paced environment
- Strong numerical and analytical aptitude, and high proficiency creating and managing advanced models

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking an Electrical Engineer to become part of a global engineering team, responsible for the design and continuous innovation of our rapidly expanding data center foot print.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud and ML/AI models running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the best possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Engineers at Amazon work to design resilient, cost effective electrical distribution systems. As engineers at Amazon we are responsible for achieving a world class uptime for our customers. We justify and communicate the technical decisions we make to Sr. Management and work hard to drive continuous advancements and improvements with our designs. As an engineer at Amazon you have the ability to drive change and define/design the systems our customers rely on.

Amazon offers a fast paced, fun, and exciting work environment. We continue to grow at exponential rates and are looking for individuals that can support our speed to market, enjoy a challenge, and have a desire for professional growth and continuous learning experiences. Amazon’s work environment is unique in every aspect and offers an exceptional opportunity for the right candidate.

If you are a creative, smart and driven individual that enjoys working with complex problems we want YOU! At Amazon you will be responsible for working on multi-million dollar designs that support our array of businesses and wide variety of customers. Great ideas are encouraged and supported. Ingenuity is the main mechanism which supports our focus on quality, speed, and cost.

We are looking for engineers with hands on electrical design experience. If you can design an electrical system, have an understanding of the critical equipment needs for a data center, and understand the constructability of varying designs you may be a good fit. As we grow we are structuring our team to own more of our engineering in house. Engineers will be responsible for taking designs from concept to the permit and construction document set. You must be capable of defining critical equipment specifications and approving equipment submittals. Engineers will directly support construction and be a part of the process from site selection review through commissioning and ultimately turnover. You will be relied on as a subject matter expert in the electrical engineering field. At Amazon we highly support continued learning opportunities and focus on continued employee development.

At Amazon team work is absolutely necessary for us to accomplish our goals. You must be able to work within a team and depend on others to accomplish the required work. As an electrical engineer at Amazon you will be working with other internal groups as well as external groups including utilities, manufacturers, vendors, and contractors.

Amazon has a global presence. As this position is based out of Virginia, travel to our head office in Seattle will be required. Travel should be up to 20% of your time, majority throughout the Virginia-based data centers and in-person collaboration efforts not in your assigned office location. International support will be part of the job, and some international travel will be necessary. Support could consist of working on international teams and could require developing schematic and design document packages. An understanding of international electrical design requirements is helpful but not necessary.

Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and we host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 14 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities of the Electrical Engineer, will be:
- Data center electrical designs and collaboration with other disciplines to create a construction document set.
- Creation of designs which meet or exceed our quality requirements and fall within our budgetary requirements.
- Work with local agencies having jurisdiction to ensure compliance with federal, state and municipal requirements and building codes.
- Review and approval of equipment submittals.
- Define project scope and provide technical support for information requests prior to, and during construction phases.
- Work with commissioning teams to properly test and validate installation, operation, and performance of electrical systems.
- Ability to work on concurrent projects in multiple geographical regions.
- Travel to sites for site review and work with onsite field engineers, as well as provide engineering evaluations, electrical systems audits, and startup as needed.
- Having fun and offering creative, out of the box solutions.

About the team
Our team also puts a high value on work-life balance. Striking a healthy balance between your personal and professional life is crucial to your happiness and success here, which is why we aren’t focused on how many hours you spend at work or online. Instead, we’re happy to offer a flexible schedule so you can have a more productive and well-balanced life—both in and outside of work.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud
platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster
a culture of inclusion that empower us to celebrate our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We have a career path for you no matter what stage you’re in when you start here. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer.
That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing
resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities experience
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel
- Experience in industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities
- Experience researching new designs, technologies, and construction methods of data center equipment and facilities

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineer License
- Experience with building codes and regulations for your region
- Experience carrying design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents
- Experience in commissioning

title: Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
This position requires in-role training at an operating site which will be 6+ weeks in duration. This training will be located 50+ miles away from the home site location. All travel accommodations for training will be booked and paid for by Amazon.

Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly employees and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key part in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Rapid and Rural Logistics (R2L) is an exciting organization within Amazon specializing in delighting our customers with speed in which we can make items appear on their doorsteps. We are a combination of operations and support teams aligned to innovate for the last mile customer experience. Come build the future with us!

Key job responsibilities
- Support, mentor, and motivate your team
- Lead large-scope projects with site and regional impact
- Create and implement productivity plans through forecast reviews, determining productivity requirements, and partnering with other Leaders to load balance
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Ops Integration, Loss Prevention and Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach, as well as continuously climb and descend stairs
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments, and grocery locations include refrigerated environments)
- Work a flexible schedule (weekends and/or overnight shifts)

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience

title: Senior Product Manager, CFX - Brazil
descriptionHtml:
Product Managers are the builders in Amazon. They own developing new features, tools, processes, and businesses for our customers, and scaling them to serve hundreds of millions of customers. PMs are focused on understanding the needs (stated or unstated) of customers, sellers, and our business and coming up with creative and often solutions to serve these needs. Think of any feature on Amazon that you like e.g. ‘Secured Delivery’, ‘Prime’, 'Easy Returns' - all these were built by product managers.


Key job responsibilities
As a Regionalization Product Manager, you will own the end-to-end strategy and execution of network regionalization to optimize cost-to-serve while protecting customer experience. You will:

Define and drive the regionalization roadmap — identify opportunities to reduce long-zone shipments, optimize fulfillment placement, and improve network efficiency across fulfillment channels (Retail, FBA, EF)
Own the P&L trade-offs — quantify CTS impact of regionalization decisions (ship COGS, split rates, UPB), model scenarios, and make data-driven recommendations balancing cost, speed, and selection availability
Work cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Transportation, CX, and Tech teams to design and launch regionalization initiatives — from ASIN-level placement rules to zone-reduction programs
Develop and manage mechanisms to track regionalization performance (CPU, split rates, long-zone share, leakage), identify root causes of deviation, and drive corrective actions
Influence senior leadership — present business cases, trade-off analyses, and program updates to L8+ stakeholders with clear metrics, risks, and asks
Lead through ambiguity — navigate complex dependencies across multiple teams, define the problem space, and drive alignment where no playbook exists.

descriptionHtml:

title: ID - Rack Lifecycle Tech, Rack Lifecycle Team
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of hardware and network engineers, logistics specialists, security and safety experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We are looking for a detail-oriented, technically skilled Rack Lifecycle Tech to join our Rack Lifecycle Team within AWS Infrastructure Operations. In this individual contributor role, you will be a hands-on executor responsible for the physical installation, cabling, handoff, and decommissioning of racks across your assigned data center site. You are the person on the floor who turns capacity plans into operational reality.

As an Rack Lifecycle Tech, you will execute structured cabling, rack installation, and decommission activities with precision and to standard — following established SOPs, escalating deviations to your team lead, and ensuring every rack you touch is installed correctly, cabled to specification, fully documented, and handed off with zero blockers, prepare SOP’s with new processes, stake holder management with cross functional teams. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities.


Key job responsibilities
🔷 Rack Installation & Cabling
· Execute rack installations including physical placement, power connections, grounding, and cable management per AWS standards and MOPs
· Perform structured cabling including fiber/copper terminations, patch panel connections, labeling, and dressing to specification
· Complete OTDR and power testing; validate results against acceptance thresholds; escalate failures to team lead promptly rather than self-resolving outside approved procedures
· Follow all EHS protocols, lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and safe work practices during installation activities
🔷 Rack Lifecycle Operations
· Execute work orders and tasks assigned by the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager under direct manager direction, maintaining accurate status updates in workflow management tools (e.g., Boost, MARS)
· Perform quality checks on completed cabling work including port map verification, label accuracy, and as-built documentation updates in CMDB/DCIM
· Identify and escalate issues, blockers, or deviations from SOPs encountered during task execution to the team lead or manager promptly; do not self-resolve outside approved procedures
· Support deployment wave readiness by participating in pre-work site walks, material staging, and tool preparation
🔷 Material Handling & Supply Chain Support
· Receive, verify, and stage incoming rack, cable, optics, and hardware deliveries; validate against BOM and flag discrepancies
· Maintain accurate site inventory records for cables, optics, patch cords, and consumables used during deployments
· Support cycle count activities and assist in identifying inventory shortfalls that may impact deployment timelines
🔷 Handover & Documentation
· Complete all required as-built documentation, port maps, test result records, and workflow sign-offs before handoff to Data Center Operations
· Update CMDB/DCIM and IPAM records accurately following rack installation or decommission activities
· Ensure handoffs are clean and fully documented with zero open blockers, enabling smooth transition to the next lifecycle phase
🔷 Rack Decommissioning
· Execute physical decommission activities per assigned MOPs — including cable removal, power disconnects, asset de-tagging, and rack extraction
· Perform device wipe and media destruction in compliance with AWS Secure Media Destruction and EHS policies
· Sort, label, and stage recovered assets (optics, cables, PDUs, hardware) for RMA, redeployment, or secure disposal per AWS Reverse Logistics policy
· Update DCIM/CMDB, IPAM, and port maps post-decom to ensure accurate space, power, and circuit records
· Validate that reclaimed U-space, power, and cooling capacity is accurately recorded in the available pool
🔷 Quality, Safety & Compliance
· Adhere to all site-level SOPs, quality standards, and governance frameworks for cabling, installation, and decommission activities
· Complete all required safety training and certifications; participate in regular EHS audits and team safety briefings
· Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying recurring quality issues, suggesting process improvements, and sharing feedback with the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager
· Use Rack Lifecycle Team tooling (e.g., Boost, MARS, ALM/DCLM) accurately to record work, track assets, and maintain data integrity
🔷 Cross-Team Coordination
· Support coordination with DCO, DCEO, Network Engineering, and facilities teams during active deployment or decom activities under manager guidance to ensure smooth execution
· Participate in daily stand-ups and pre-work briefings; communicate clearly on task status, blockers, and schedule adherence
· Provide accurate, timely updates on task completion and flag risks or delays to the team lead immediately
🔷 Continuous Learning & Development
· Maintain and develop technical proficiency in structured cabling, fiber optics, rack installation, and data center physical infrastructure
· Complete required certifications and training modules including EHS, LOTO, and any Rack Lifecycle Team-specific technical programs
· Proactively seek feedback from leads and managers to improve personal performance and output quality
· Support the onboarding and training of new team members; share knowledge and best practices with peers to build overall team capability and quality standards
· Stay current on AWS infrastructure tooling, cabling standards, and process updates communicated by the Rack Lifecycle Team


A day in the life
As a Rack Lifecycle Tech, your day is on the data center floor. You might start the morning by reviewing your assigned work orders in Boost, checking in with your team lead on priorities, and staging cables and optics for a rack installation wave. By midday, you could be terminating fiber runs at a patch panel, running OTDR tests to validate loss results against acceptance thresholds, or labeling and dressing a freshly installed rack. In the afternoon, you might be updating CMDB records for completed work orders, de-tagging and staging recovered assets from an EOL decom, or helping onboard a new technician by walking them through the SOP. If you encounter a deviation from the approved MOP, you escalate it to your team lead immediately — you don't improvise. Your role is hands-on, technical, and precise — you execute the work that keeps AWS capacity on track.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and Amazon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of computer networking experience
- 1+ years of Linux operating systems experience
- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field
- Experience in computer networking
- Experience working with Linux operating systems
- Can lift and rack equipment up to 40 pounds
- Experience with computer hardware troubleshooting and repair

Preferred qualifications

- Can work in cramped spaces or in elevated locations while adhering to health & safety guidelines
- Experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure
- Experience managing work and priorities through a ticketing system
- Experience with cabling infrastructure best practices and methodologies
- Experience working in a data center environment (racking and stacking gear, cable management, hot/cold aisle containment)
- Familiarity with rack decommissioning including device wipe, media destruction, and asset recovery procedures
