title: Senior Financial Analyst, Global Procurement Finance
descriptionHtml:
How does Amazon continue to grow its capacity to deliver for customers in new ways? What new types of operations will Amazon add to its portfolio as it innovates order fulfillment and delivery standards across North America and emerging markets? How can Amazon become best in class in operational excellence?

Who we are: Global Procurement Organization Finance (GPOF) is dedicated to answering the questions above, which drive the Amazon flywheel. The GPOF team validates procurement methodologies, supports vendor negotiations and strategy, and delivers analysis to identify controls and risks opportunities and benefits impacting category management and procurement operations. We are looking for a curious person who wants to learn, develop and grow. The candidate will collaborate with many procurement colleagues and is a trustworthy business partner for our engineering teams. You value diversity, have fun on the job and want to be part of a growing company and team.

Team Exposure: This role collaborates closely with a broad range of global finance and business leaders in Procurement, Engineering, Construction, and Operations teams towards controllership and risk functions. The role also partners with stakeholders across technical projects & software development teams, capital planning, compliance, risks and controls. This role involves driving initiatives, collecting, analyzing and managing quantitative data and creating meaningful reports to lead business improvement and driving controls and policy compliance across the global procurement organization. This role also maintains project oversight, drives initiatives and policy reviews and partners with category management on strategic input drivers to continuously improve the scalability and efficiency of the procurement organization.

Success in this role: The successful candidate has demonstrated the following abilities: they drive strategic decisions and provide thought leadership to influence senior business owners, while challenging assumptions and plans with data-driven recommendations. They navigate ambiguous environments independently and design long-term solutions with limited guidance. They collaborate effectively with executives and various business units across Amazon, building trust through expertise and high judgment. They bring superior verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex finance issues to non-Finance senior partners and adjust their style based on audience. A typical day in this role provides an opportunity to innovate by architecting creative solutions with large-scale data mining tools, identifying strategic priorities that drive long-term value, and solving significantly complex problems that impact company-wide decisions. They lead initiatives that may be undefined and work across organizations to implement scalable solutions. The role requires demonstrated expertise in determining where to simplify or extend solutions for optimal outcomes, while effectively balancing short-term versus long-term needs.

About the role: Amazon is seeking a Finance Manager within Global Procurement Operations Finance to own and drive strategic initiatives that shape global procurement decisions. This role will independently lead high-impact, business-critical processes with significant visibility to senior leadership, including frequent interactions with Directors within Operations and Finance. You will develop and implement robust financial controls while building and maintaining strategic partnerships across multiple organizations, including Operations business teams, engineering services, and Finance teams throughout Worldwide Operations. You will lead complex financial analyses and modeling efforts that drive strategic decision-making, while architecting and implementing scalable solutions that enhance planning/reporting mechanisms. The role involves identifying and driving long-term investment strategies and cost optimization opportunities across the Fulfillment Center network, while managing multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously. Success in this role requires the ability to navigate ambiguous environments, challenge assumptions with data-driven insights, and influence cross-functional stakeholders to drive meaningful change.

title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Networks
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about building systems that keep one of the world's largest networks running? We're looking for a Software Development Engineer to join a team that builds traffic engineering and fast-reroute solutions for the AWS global backbone network — the infrastructure behind S3, EC2, Direct Connect, and every AWS service.

In this role, you'll design and build software that detects congestion and failures across 400+ global sites and automatically reroutes traffic to healthier paths. You'll work at the intersection of distributed systems and networking, solving problems that directly impact the reliability and performance of AWS for millions of customers.

You'll be part of a hybrid team of software, systems development, and network engineers across the US and Australia. This position is based in Seattle and sits at the heart of AWS global networking.

Why you'll love it here:
-You'll work on problems that few teams in the world get to tackle — steering traffic for the entire AWS backbone
-Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we genuinely invest in mentorship — through 1:1 pairing, kind code reviews, and projects tailored to your growth
-We care about your career: we assign work based on what will help you develop as an engineer, not just what needs shipping next

Key job responsibilities
-Design, build, and maintain software services that steer traffic across the AWS global backbone network
-Develop and extend traffic engineering controllers that detect congestion and failures in real time and automatically reroute traffic to healthier paths
-Write clean, well-tested code in a production environment where availability directly impacts AWS customers
-Contribute to system design discussions — from API design to data modelling to choosing the right trade-offs for scale and reliability
-Build and improve monitoring, alerting, and automation tooling to give the team better visibility into network health
-Collaborate with network engineers, systems engineers, and partner teams to translate operational needs into software solutions
-Participate in code reviews, providing thoughtful and constructive feedback to teammates
Participate in on-call rotations (typically one week every two months), working with the team to resolve issues and fix root causes
-Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, or improve existing systems and processes

A day in the life
You'll spend most of your time building software that gives us visibility and control over traffic across the AWS backbone. On any given day you might be designing a new feature, reviewing a teammate's code, or debugging issues. You'll work closely with network engineers and partner teams — a lot of what you build is about detecting problems and mitigating them before customers notice. Beyond coding, you'll join design discussions and on-call rotations. The work mixes building new things with keeping existing systems reliable at massive scale.

About the team
We build the systems that keep traffic flowing across the AWS global backbone — connecting every region and edge location worldwide. Our network grows ~70% year-on-year, so the problems we solve constantly evolve. The team is distributed across the US and Australia, and this role is based in Seattle. We have a broad mix of experience levels and backgrounds, and we genuinely value mentorship and knowledge sharing. What matters most is curiosity and a willingness to solve hard problems.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Salesforce Developer, Amazon Web Services (AWS)
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Field Experience (AFX) team builds go-to-market tooling that gives the AWS sales and marketing organization superpowers, helping them focus on customers instead of manual processes. As a Salesforce Developer, System Development Engineer II on AFX, you will design and deliver the Salesforce-based systems that power contracting, approval workflows, and deal management for the AWS field. You will build on the Salesforce platform (Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Flows, and platform APIs) and integrate it with distributed services and LLM-powered automation that operate at AWS scale.

Salesforce is at the center of how AWS moves deals from opportunity to signed, executed contract, and large language models are redefining how we support that work. This is your chance to help shape that transformation. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, writing high-quality Apex and LWC code, contributing to system and data-model design, and collaborating with partners across the AWS partner business, deal desk, legal, finance, and solutions architecture teams.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build Salesforce applications and APIs (Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Flows, and platform integrations) that power contracting, approval workflows, and deal management for one of the largest field sales organizations in the world, covering the full lifecycle from design through deployment and operations.
- Develop and optimize approval-flow and workflow-orchestration logic on the Salesforce platform, including multi-stage routing, delegation, escalation, and gate enforcement, that keeps contracting fast, compliant, and fully auditable.
- Build and maintain integrations between Salesforce and external systems, synchronizing deal and account data across systems at scale and improving data quality and coverage.
- Implement LLM-powered workflows and automation that reduce manual effort for the sales field and generate actionable insights from complex contracting and account data.
- Participate actively in code reviews, providing constructive feedback that raises engineering standards, and mentor other engineers through documentation, training, and pairing sessions.
- Identify root causes of operational issues and drive permanent fixes, while collaborating with stakeholders across deal desk, legal, finance, the AWS partner business, and solutions architects to ensure your solutions meet real customer needs.


A day in the life
You start by reviewing pull requests from teammates (Apex classes and LWC components), offering detailed feedback that helps everyone grow. Mid-morning, you dig into a feature in the approval-flow logic, writing Apex and pairing with a colleague to work through a tricky integration between Salesforce and a downstream AWS services. After lunch, you join a design discussion with solutions architects about how an LLM-powered workflow can reduce manual steps for the field team. Later, you investigate an operational alert on a contracting flow, trace it to its root cause, and ship a lasting fix. You move between focused coding and cross-team collaboration with partners in deal desk, legal, and the partner business.


About the team
The AFX teams sit within AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services and build the infrastructure that supports the sales field and AWS customers at massive scale. This team owns the Salesforce-based contracting and approval-workflow platform, the systems that take a deal from opportunity to signed, executed contract. Our closest partners span deal desk, legal, finance, the AWS partner business, and solutions architecture organizations. We are investing heavily in LLM-driven tooling and large-scale data processing to redefine how go-to-market and contracting teams operate. If you want to build Salesforce systems that directly shape how AWS engages and contracts with its customers worldwide, this is the team for you.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience in automating, deploying, and supporting large-scale infrastructure
- Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Python, Ruby, Golang, Java, C++, C#, Rust
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines build processes
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience working in an Agile environment

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with distributed systems at scale

descriptionHtml:

We're looking for an ambitious team member who will bring added scientific rigor and innovation to how our customer's experience security with and through open source software. Our systems operate on a global scale across a diverse ecosystem of field teams, security requirements, and tooling which requires high velocity security innovation that scales.

We are seeking an Applied Scientist to help define, design, build, and operate AI-powered security solutions across the full lifecycle of open source software usage.  You will work alongside a team to build intelligent automation that augments manual identification, analysis, and remediation workflows, enforces security controls for agents and human experts, and provides data-driven insights to AWS leadership.

Key job responsibilities
- Architect and build AI-powered security applications and tooling — Design and implement LLM-based systems (leveraging Bedrock, SageMaker, and state of the art patterns) for intelligent code scanning, automated solution development/deployment, and remediation alternatives. 
- Transform manual processes – Reimagine and deliver change from low throughput, human-dependent processes into high volume, machine speed pipelines without sacrificing key quality metrics. 
- Collaborate with and influence other leaders – The open source ecosystem has many stakeholders, and change requires listening and supporting but also influencing and leading through action. 
- Drive proactive security automation — Build systems that identify and remediate security issues in deliverables (code, threat models, content) without requiring explicit builder consent at every step, moving from reactive reviews to proactive prevention 
- Own operational excellence — Define and maintain SLAs, monitoring, alerting, runbooks, and incident response for services you own; participate in on-call rotation to support 24/7 availability

title: Software Development Engineer , Leo Regulus
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is bringing satellite internet to 100+ countries — and before we can sell in any of them, an enormous amount of behind-the-scenes checking has to pass: is every customer charged correctly, is tax right for that country's laws, does money move to the right accounts, are the invoices legally valid, does the whole buy-and-activate experience actually work end to end? Today, dozens of teams work through this by hand, one step after another, for months. It's the single biggest thing standing between "we're ready" and "we've launched" — and we're replacing that entire process with AI.

Leo Regulus is an AI-native team building squads of autonomous agents that compress Leo's launch process from months to days. The agents run in parallel, share context across every domain a launch touches — tax, accounting, payments, legal, trade, and commerce — and get smarter with each country we ship. Crucially, we don't do the manual work; we build the agents that do it, and do it better each time. Instead of writing the checks by hand, we build agents that write, run, diagnose, and fix them.

This is a rare kind of problem: real autonomy with real stakes — these agents gate a global product launch — and genuine cross-domain reasoning, because a single launch spans law, finance, payments, and the shopping experience all at once, and the agents have to keep each other in sync. You don't need any background in testing or launch operations; you need to be great at building intelligent systems and excited by agentic AI as the product itself — designing how agents plan, act, check their own work, recover from failure, and learn. If building the AI team that launches satellite internet across the planet — in minutes instead of months — sounds like the most interesting thing you could work on, let's talk.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
Key Job Responsibilities:

*Design and build autonomous AI agents that execute end-to-end ecommerce validation without human intervention
- Build orchestration systems that coordinate dozens of domain-specific agents working in parallel
- Create knowledge base architectures that ground agent behavior in accounting, tax, and compliance rules
- Solve novel problems at the intersection of AI, distributed systems, and financial domain complexity


A day in the life
An SDE on Leo Regulus will be responsible for designing, building, and operating autonomous AI agent systems that automate the end-to-end ecommerce launch lifecycle — from requirements generation through financial configuration, test execution, and validation — enabling Amazon Leo to scale country and feature launches across 100+ markets without proportional headcount growth.

About the team
We are a team building the AI infrastructure that makes Amazon Leo's 100-country launch possible. Our entire stack is AI-native — every system we build either is an agent, powers an agent, or feeds an agent. We don't maintain legacy test frameworks or manual runbooks. We build autonomous systems and point them at problems that would otherwise require hundreds of engineers.

title: Software Engineer, S3 Discovery
descriptionHtml:
Managing trillions of objects in storage, retrieving them in sub-x ms, building software that deploys to tens of thousands of hosts, achieving 99.999999999% (you didn’t read that wrong, that’s 11 nines!) durability. These are just a few of the numbers that give you a sense of the scale of the exciting problems you will find every day working in Simple Storage Service (S3). Amazon S3 powers businesses across e globe that make the lives of consumers better daily. Whether its electronic content delivered to your home, technology that betters your remote working experience, allows you to plan travel to exotic places or simply get stuff delivered to your home.

As a Software Development Engineer in the S3 Distribution Plane team, you will deliver services at scale to delight our customers and support the routing of billions of requests per minute to S3’s globally distributed server fleet. You will have the opportunity to design and develop systems and services in the domains of DNS, IP and Network Connectivity, TLS Certificates, VPC Endpoints and Private Connectivity. You will work alongside engineers and leaders who obsess about operations, performance, availability, scalability, and durability of customer data. Our services run at scale worldwide and as a member of this team, you will have the opportunity to ship code often, and see the impact your code has on a wide range of S3 customers.

Day to day you will be responsible for designing, delivering and maintaining the operational health of our services, maintaining our build & release systems, and ensuring maximum up-time for our developers and customers. You will provide coaching and mentoring for junior engineers and participate in design reviews, operations meetings and leadership discussions. You will partner with service teams across AWS to build ground-breaking DNS, networking and security solutions in code for S3. You will work closely with the likes of Amazon Route 53, AWS EC2 and AWS Networking to achieve the combined goals of AWS and S3. You will transcend a single organization in order to deliver solutions that require broader integration across AWS. For this reason, thinking big and thinking outside of S3 is one of the key tenets you will have to practise on a daily basis.

As a Software Development Engineer in our team, you are constantly striving to raise our operational bar and improve our infrastructure, enabling our teams to move faster. Your responsibilities will include:

Developing tools to streamline operations as we scale to reduce operational load and improve our overall operational posture. Influencing & driving operational excellence and best practices within the organization.

Identifying ways to increase the automate and improve our test infrastructure and make our CI/CD more robust and flexible.

Playing a key role in investigating and recommending best practices for maintaining and improving code quality, fleet health, and security & reliability of our service.

Growing our talent through actively mentor junior system development engineers, improving their skills, their knowledge of our systems, and their ability to get things done.

Sharing your knowledge with wider teams and writing clear and concise documentation to allow other system development engineers to get the most out of the service and tools.

Our team works together to provide work/life balance for all team members. We recognize that the circumstances of our team members vary, and we balance work across the team so that we’re all able to maintain high standards on behalf of our customers, while at the same time allowing for rich and happy personal lives.

In AWS, if you build it, you own it. S3 is a highly available 7x24 worldwide service requiring dedicated support from our engineering teams. We pride ourselves on a high level of ownership in the work we do. This means we hold a high bar for test automation, verification processes, design and code reviews to ensure that our systems meet the exacting standards our customers demand. We maintain a regular on-call rotation across our teams with engineers and managers all taking part to resolve the inevitable issues that arise. We work hard to minimize getting paged in the middle of the night as we recognize that a well-rested employee is a productive employee.

Upon joining S3, every employee is paired with a peer buddy who will help you to quickly come up to speed in understanding the technology we’re building, the tools we use and the business problems we’re trying to solve. We hire exceptional people and we recognize the importance of coaching others. We have a formal mentor search application that lets you find a mentor that works best for you based on location, job family, and job level. On our internal “Broadcast” video streaming website, you’ll find countless presentations by some of the brightest minds in computing discussing solutions to many of the exciting problems we’re solving in AWS today with new live-streaming videos added every week.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 14 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

Work/Life Balance
Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility in working hours and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.

Mentorship & Career Growth
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Our members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded engineer and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

title: Software Development Manager, AIO Visualization and Reporting
descriptionHtml:
AWS customers commit to billions of dollars of Savings Plans and Reserved Instances to cut their bills by up to 72%. Tens of thousands of Amazon employees use this team's tools to execute those purchases, correct billing information, and keep the commitments accurate. We are looking for a Software Development Manager to lead the nine engineers who own them.

The scope covers two distinct areas. One is the commitment lifecycle: creating, modifying, and refunding customer commitments, and making sure the resulting numbers are correct everywhere they are reported. The other is the internal billing platform and the authorization service in front of it, which decides who is allowed to see which customer's data, millions of times a month. A senior engineer leads each area, and a product manager works across both, so you will lead through your engineers rather than assigning every task yourself.

The team inherited five services in the space of seven months, each below the bar for operational hygiene. Since then it has cut open security findings by 97%, closed the monitoring gaps that had let a data quality defect run undetected for months, and generally improved operational hygiene. What is left is the interesting work: replacing a deployment pipeline that has become the single biggest tax on the team's velocity, retiring end-of-life frameworks that predate 2015, and building the data auditing that a financial system of this size should have had from the beginning. You will do that while delivering funded commitments the business is counting on, including a new payment method with material financial impact for the business and the automation of a refund process that today runs on spreadsheets and manual safeguards.

There is also a strategic question waiting for whoever takes this role. Today the team maintains the access rules governing who may view customer billing data, and it executes 220+ document-based operating procedures on behalf of Legal, Finance, Sales, and Customer Support. The team owns the tooling but not the policies, which means it absorbs a steady stream of decisions it has no business context to make. Inverting that model is a design problem worth years of leverage, and it is yours to define.

We are looking for somebody to put their stamp on this team and decide what it becomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the charter, roadmap, and multi-year architecture across both areas. Decide what gets built, what gets decommissioned, and in what order.
- Directly hire, coach, and develop engineers from entry level through senior. Two positions are already open, and you will define what they are.
- Delegate component and operational ownership to your senior engineers, and grow them as leaders rather than becoming the decision bottleneck.
- Be accountable for the operational health of financially material services: security posture, deployment health, monitoring, and the audit mechanisms that prove your numbers are right.
- Balance funded business delivery against the modernization the platform needs, and be able to defend that sequencing to senior leadership.
- Represent the team in weekly operational reviews and in your organization's annual planning process.
- Build the relationships that make the work possible, with product management, with the operations teams who use your tools every day, and with partner engineering teams across AWS.

A day in the life
Most days split four ways: unblocking your team, following up on something affecting a customer or an internal operator, hiring and coaching, and thinking past the current quarter. You will spend real time in design reviews and in the details of your systems, because the judgment calls in this space are technical ones. You will also spend real time writing, because the decisions that matter here are argued in documents and reviewed by people several levels above you.


About the team
You will join the AWS Insights organization, which helps customers understand what they spend, forecast what they will spend, optimize the cost of what they run, and get alerted when costs surprise them. This team sits at the financial core of that mission. The work is unusually concrete: when it goes well, customers save money and internal operators stop doing things by hand.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of engineering team management experience
- 7+ years of working directly within engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 8+ years of leading the definition and development of multi tier web services experience
- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in recruiting, hiring, mentoring/coaching and managing teams of Software Engineers to improve their skills, and make them more effective, product software engineers
- Experience in communicating with users, other technical teams, and senior leadership to collect requirements, describe software product features, technical designs, and product strategy

title: Senior Product Manager - Technical, Region Flexibility & Efficiency
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Product Manager - Technical (PMT), Region Flexibility & Efficiency, you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for helping Amazon businesses operate against constrained resources while improving the efficiency and scale of our business. Working backwards from customer and business needs, you will define the end-state architecture that lets services break region coupling while retaining the ability to keep critical business functions within a region. You will also reduce the builder effort required to execute efficiency initiatives by delivering Agentic AI and headless solutions that connect the disparate tools across Amazon's ecosystem.

We are looking for a passionate, deeply technical, and customer-obsessed leader to define the Region Flexibility & Efficiency product and set the technical direction for fundamental architectural changes across the entire Amazon software stack. You will own the "what" and the "why": defining the customer problem, writing the narratives (PRFAQ, PRD) that align the organization, making data-driven prioritization and trade-off decisions, and defining the success metrics the initiative is measured against. You will partner closely with the engineering and program teams who own delivery, and influence architectural change across thousands of teams without direct authority.

- Own the multi-year product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Region Flexibility & Efficiency, and secure alignment from engineering teams and senior leadership.
- Work backwards from customers and businesses to define requirements, and author the narrative documents (PRFAQ, PRD, product/technical specs) that drive decisions.
- Define the target architecture and technical direction in partnership with principal engineers, evaluating trade-offs across latency, resiliency, cost, and complexity.
- Define and track the metrics that measure product success, and use data to prioritize the roadmap and make build/no-build decisions.
- Influence architectural change across thousands of teams, and communicate the product vision to audiences ranging from individual developers to senior leaders.

About the team
The Region Flexibility & Efficiency (RFE) organization drives the optimization and resilience of Amazon's global infrastructure. We own programs that shape how Amazon operates across AWS regions, from enabling services to run flexibly across regions to driving petabyte-scale efficiency improvements that directly influence Amazon's infrastructure investment decisions.

Our portfolio spans infrastructure optimization programs, multi-region capacity strategy, fleet intelligence platforms, and agentic AI capabilities that automate performance improvements across hundreds of engineering teams. We support Amazon businesses including Stores, Prime Video, Alexa, and Kindle, and partner closely with AWS teams to improve both internal capabilities and public offerings.

This is a small, high-leverage team where individual contributors have direct impact at the highest levels of leadership. We value technical depth, hands-on execution, and the ability to operate across organizational boundaries. With millions of customers depending on Amazon's infrastructure every day, we build solutions that are robust, scalable, and designed to "just work" at Amazon's full scale.

- Bachelor's degree

- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product

title: Sr. Customer Delivery Engineer (CDE), Global Enterprise Services (GES)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

As part of Global Enterprise Services (GES), the Customer Delivery Engineer (CDE) for Amazon Leo serves as the primary technical authority and trusted advisor for customers integrating with the Leo. This role bridges the gap between customer needs and Amazon Leo's technical capabilities, driving successful implementation, managing integration activities, and ensuring long-term customer success. You will deliver architectural guidance to customers, lead complex implementation and configuration activities through hands-on engagement, and provide technical advice to business development and internal teams.
As a CDE, you will engage customers from contract execution, guiding them through the full lifecycle of network and back-office integration, from initial architecture design, implementation and deployment of system configurations, and development of code and scripts that optimize and automate functions to meet customer needs, through testing and the establishment of an ongoing support funnel across the post-sales organization. You will operate at the intersection of networking, cloud services, back-office and business systems, and customer enablement, providing hands-on technical guidance that accelerates customer time-to-value with Amazon Leo.
Beyond standard onboarding, you are the hands-on delivery engine of Amazon Leo Professional Services. You own the paid statement of work (SOW)-based practice for complex, custom, and enterprise-scale engagements that fall outside the included services. You will scope and deliver bespoke integration, multi-region rollouts, and system migrations, often working as an internal resource or together with partners under fixed-fee or time-and-materials engagements, owning the specific work that only Amazon Leo can provide (Leo Console, terminal and customer-terminal provisioning, LEO network integration, and cloud/private connectivity). You will focus on the deep, complex L300–L400 tier of work (mobility, original equipment manufacturer [OEM] integration, and bespoke architecture) while directing and overseeing Professional Services partners who carry scaled, repeatable implementation under Amazon Leo's SOW and quality governance.
You will work with Customer Delivery Managers (CDMs) and Technical Program Managers (TPMs) on customer onboarding activities, collaborating with Product Managers, Engineering, and Solutions Architects to represent external customers’ needs. Join a team that values innovation and builds the automation tools and processes that accelerate customer delivery at scale.


Key job responsibilities
• Represent Amazon Leo as the technical expert during customer onboarding, leading detailed design decisions and performing hands-on implementation of complex and scalable integrations.
• Collaborate with stakeholders to gather detailed requirements and propose effective integration plans; provide guidance and troubleshooting support throughout the technical implementation process.
• Represent Amazon Leo in design and technical review meetings with customer stakeholders, providing technical guidance and recommendations on technology solutions and best practices.
• Design and develop code and API scripts, working backwards with customers from broadly defined problems and user stories. Support customers with planning, troubleshooting, and deployment of the software modules that meet their back-office integration and automation requirements.
• Provide on-site and remote support to customers during demonstrations, training sessions, trials, workshops, and systems deployment planning meetings; support on-site customer meetings to complete final design for custom network and back-office integrations.
• Represent Amazon Leo during customer testing and validation, collaborating with internal and external stakeholders on testing procedures and infrastructure, and supporting on-site or remote testing until final customer acceptance is achieved.
• Scope and deliver paid, SOW-based Professional Services engagements, bespoke integration, multi-region rollouts, and migrations, as fixed-fee or time-and-materials projects, producing a scoped deliverable with a defined end date and handing off the repeatable pattern to ongoing support.
• Apply the advisory-versus-build operating rule that governs Professional Services: advisory work (guiding, recommending, answering questions) stays within included scope, while hands-on-keyboard build of a deliverable outside included scope is qualified, scoped, and delivered as a paid engagement, run in parallel so it never delays go-live.
• Direct and oversee Professional Services partners, whether subcontracted through AWS ProServ or external (third-party) partners under an Amazon Leo SOW, ensuring delivery meets Amazon Leo's technical bar and quality-governance standards while retaining ownership of specific IP.
• Work with sector and core GES leads to guide engineering activities, define baseline operational runbooks, plan automation, coordinate development of tooling and mechanisms, and share knowledge across the organization through mentoring, training, and reusable artifacts.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life
You work alongside CDMs and TPMs with internal and customer technical staff to create custom connectivity solutions that meet enterprise requirements, integrating Leo capabilities with associated networking, AWS/Cloud, and specialized equipment. You provide hands-on technical expertise across the full system lifecycle (concept, design, installation, test, operation, and maintenance), ensuring the logical and systematic conversion of customer requirements into total-system solutions that meet technical, schedule, and cost constraints. On any given engagement, you might be scoping a paid statement of work for a bespoke back-office integration, drawing the line between what is included advisory and what is billable build, and standing behind a certified partner or AWS Professional Services team delivering regional rollout at scale, all while keeping the customer on their go-live path. You will identify areas to invent, refine, and automate to reduce manual operations and fulfill the requirements of the business long-term and its customers.

About the team
The GES Service Delivery team connects Product, Engineering, and Operations to direct customer context, ensuring Leo services reach enterprise customers in a form they can consume, trust, and scale. To internal teams, GES is the voice of the customer: surfacing field gaps, integration friction, and deployment-scale issues that shape engineering priorities. To account teams, GES is the technical readiness authority, providing clear, current assessments of what is ready and what it takes to close gaps before customer conversations begin. GES Service Delivery leads the Amazon Leo B2B Professional Services, a paid delivery practice pairing Leo experts with AWS Professional Services and certified partners to deliver complex work at scale. As a CDE, you will represent the technical depth of the Leo Service Delivery team, collaborating across Product, Engineering, Customer Delivery, and Customer Care to deliver a customer-obsessed experience.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of architecting/operating solutions built on any cloud service provider like Azure, AWS, GCP, OCI, etc. experience
- Experience scripting in modern program languages, or experience operating highly available, distributed systems of data extraction, ingestion, and processing of large data sets
- Experience in delivering customer engagements in a professional services role
- Experience writing and publishing technical documents or equivalent
- Experience leading system integration, deployment and testing activities
- 3+ years of IP network and architecture design

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in network fundamentals (DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, routing, switching, HTTP)
- Experience directing or overseeing third-party system integrators or delivery partners against a defined quality bar
- Experience with System Integration as a Systems Engineer or similar role, preferably in wireless cellular or satellite technology

The role will also help connect customers with experts who can provide them the most accurate and up-to-date information about their packages. The work is beyond fulfilling and delivering customer orders; it’s making sure we put smiles on customer’s faces.

Key job responsibilities
As a Delivery Station Customer Service Associate, you will be responsible for:
• Communicating with customers directly in-person, in addition to communicating via phone and email
• Empathizing with and prioritizing customer needs
• Upholding company values and respecting every customer
• Resolving issues and setting appropriate expectations with customers
• Clearly understanding and responding appropriately to the issues that customers present

A day in the life

As orders are dispatched and delivered, you’ll be in contact with our warehouse, associates, delivery partners and customers when they need guidance. Where a customer needs to reschedule a delivery, you’ll be informing our delivery partners. Operating at the heart of Amazon’s logistics, you’ll develop logistical and customer expertise that sets Amazon apart. You’ll connect with our customers every day, using your in-depth understanding of our supply chain and local knowledge of delivery connections and warehouses.

title: Senior Product Design Electrical Engineer, Data Center Engineering - Electrical Products and Services (DCE-EPS)
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services is hiring a Senior Product Design Electrical Engineer with diesel generator experience for our Electrical Products and Services team. The Electrical Products and Services Team is a AWS's Data Center Engineering global engineering team, responsible for the design and continuous innovation for products used within our rapidly expanding data center footprint.

The Electrical Products and Services team works to design and develop resilient, cost-effective electrical distribution products and systems. As an engineer at Amazon, we are responsible for achieving world class uptime for our customers. We drive continuous advancements and improvements with our designs and communicate technical direction to Senior Leadership. We seek new ways to enhance the reliability, scalability, and cost effectiveness of our engineering designs. As an engineer at Amazon, you can design, innovate, and improve the products our customers rely on.

Amazon offers a fast-paced, fun, and exciting work environment. We continue to grow at exponential rates and are looking for individuals that can support our speed to market, enjoy a challenge, and have a desire for professional growth and continuous learning experiences. Amazon’s work environment is unique in every aspect and offers an exceptional opportunity for the right candidate.

If you are a natural leader, smart and worked with high performing team of engineers that enjoys working with complex problems we want you! At Amazon, you will be responsible for working on product designs and supporting our wide variety of customers. Great ideas are encouraged and supported. Ingenuity is the main mechanism which supports our focus on quality, speed, and cost.

At Amazon, teamwork is absolutely necessary for us to accomplish our goals. You must be able to work within a team and depend on others to accomplish the required work. As a product engineer at Amazon, you will be working with other internal groups as well as external groups including engineering service providers, manufacturers, vendors, inspectors, third party testing labs and contractors.

Amazon has a global presence. Travel will be necessary but shouldn’t be more than 30%. International support will be part of the job, and some international travel may be necessary. Your contribution could consist of leading international projects and could require developing engineering information packages. An understanding of international electrical product design requirements is helpful but not necessary.



Key job responsibilities

• Work with internal partner teams to solicit customer input and define design requirements for product design.
• Lead new product design, development and qualification of critical electrical power distribution equipment for AWS data centers with primary focus on backup power generation, specifically diesel generators, enclosures, and aftertreatment systems, as well as connecting dependencies with other electrical equipment.
• Work with global suppliers and manufacturers to specify appropriate equipment and components, ensuring tier 2-3 supply chain resiliency.
• Ensure compliance with UL, CSA, IEC and federal, state and municipal requirements and building codes across different countries through appropriate levels of testing.
• Validate design through prototype, pre-production and first-of-kind builds, conducting DFx and value engineering analysis through each step and updating design and documentation.
• Work with field engineering and commissioning teams to properly test and validate installation, operation, and performance of electrical products.
• Ability to provide support for manufacturing activities for the new products on concurrent projects in multiple geographical locations.
• Be a leader within the product development team as well as within internal and external teams that support the data center.


About the team

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

*Diverse Experiences*
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field
- Knowledge of critical data center mechanical and electrical equipment
- Experience developing solutions and executing plans on complex projects
- Experience researching new designs, technologies, and construction methods of data center equipment and facilities

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineering or Architectural License
- Knowledge of building codes and regulations for your region
- Experience carrying design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents

Operating across Australia & New Zealand, India, North Asia, and Southeast Asia, APAC CDS manages 41 leased/owned sites and supports global follow-the-sun operations. APAC CDS covers three core disciplines: deployments (control systems in new data centers), projects (capital improvement works at live sites), and service (control systems at live sites), with additional specializations in colocated sites, systems engineering, controls fleet, program management, and coordination.

- Ability and willingness to collaborate with peers around the globe, which may involve some participation in meetings at odd hours
- Ability and willingness to travel domestically or globally as and when needed

Controls Deployment & Service (CDS) Engineers deliver and support data center building automation systems, such as Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS). CDS Engineers work to deploy and service building automation systems, to ensure the health of our data centers. As a CDS Engineer, you may oversee deployment of a new BMS or EPMS as part of a new data center build, deliver projects to upgrade an existing data center owned or leased by Amazon, or deliver projects to upgrade colocated data centers with Amazon hardware. As a CDS Engineer, you may also be required to provide local servicing expertise to our fleet or data centers in your region, and occasionally assist with global support. Successfully working as a CDS Engineer will also require you to partner effectively with the many teams at Amazon that make our data center deployments and operations a success, including Construction, Commissioning, Critical Projects, Data Center Operations, Procurement, Program Management, Design, and Engineering teams, as well as maintaining strong relationships with our vendors.

- Delivery of critical projects to upgrade data center automation
- Service and support provided to partner teams, providing diagnosis and resolution of Loss of Visibility (LOV), Loss of Resilience (LOR), Large Scale Event (LSE), Critical Scale Event (CSE), and other operations impacting events
- Resolution of tasks within predefined Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
- Delivery of further initiatives to improve the efficiency of our data centers or our operations procedures

Unser Team arbeitet mit Führungskräften, Mitarbeitenden und lokalen Behörden an allen unseren Standorten zusammen, um die Einhaltung der Amazon-Richtlinien und gesetzlichen Vorschriften sicherzustellen und die Sicherheit unserer Arbeitsumgebungen zu gewährleisten. title: Senior Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
• Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes.
• Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
• Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
• Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
• Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardize processes across the EU network

A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year IRL/UK certified apprenticeship
- Relevant experience in a technical leadership role
- Relevant experience working in both electrical and mechanical disciplines
- Relevant experience in automation or material handling equipment environments
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working in a multi-contractor and multi-site working environment
- Understanding of PLC based controls systems and statutory compliance requirements
- Experience using computerised maintenance management systems to plan proactive maintenance and record reactive tasks
- A degree preferably in a technical discipline or operations

* Identify, promote and implement security best practices while effectively partnering with internal customers to evaluate current and future security needs, processes, and initiatives, incident response planning, facilitating and management.
* Domestic regional travel up to 50% of the time when applicable.
* Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach; Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts; Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud; Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments); Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs).
* This role covers 24/7 operations and must be able to work all shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays.

A day in the life
As a SLP Expert, you will join a team of S&LP professionals providing security as a service to business customers across multiple business units within a dedicated geographical area. You perform regular physical security audits and investigate policy violations, security-related incidents, and loss events. During your investigations, you will collect information by monitoring systems and tools, analyzing data reports, and conducting interviews. Your findings contribute to identifying vulnerabilities in various processes to identify and drive mitigating measures. You play a key role in maintaining the physical integrity of our sites by auditing and monitoring the health status of our systems and, jointly with subject matter experts and external suppliers, maintain their functionality. Furthermore, you identify and act upon initiatives improving our physical security infrastructure and contribute directly to the budgetary planning for our external suppliers. You interact on a daily basis with our external security service providers to ensure delivery of high-quality security services and a smooth customer experience. You will be working on multiple high-impact initiatives/projects by collaborating with stakeholders across organizational levels to deliver measurable outcomes through effective project management. Finally, you deliver loss prevention-related education and awareness programs to other teams across all management levels and manage the implementation of our S&LP plan.

About the team
Worldwide Operations Security (WWOS) is the global organization that supports field Loss Prevention and is designed to support Amazon's Worldwide Operations, as well as affiliate and retail businesses, by creating and maintaining a work environment that is both prepared and secure through global security centers of excellence staffed by subject matter experts in people and asset protection. We accomplish this by creating policy and implementation guidelines; training leadership and staff; using technology to eliminate subjectivity, complexity, and variation; identifying, preparing for, and mitigating risk; and auditing our practices to ensure compliance.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 4+ years of relevant professional or military experience
- 2+ years of security service, loss prevention, asset protection, investigations, or law enforcement, or 2+ years of Amazon (Blue Badge/FTE) experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in implementing metric-based strategies utilizing continuous improvement concepts
- Experience in physical security systems maintenance/implementation and coordinating scope of work with security vendors
- 2+ years of operational experience in risk management, audit, data analytics, inventory control, quality assurance, retail, warehouse, distribution center services, delivery service, or supply chain
- Investigative interviewing experience; Wicklander and Zulawski, Loss Prevention Qualified, Certified Protection Professional, Loss Prevention Certified, Certified Forensic Interviewer, Certified Threat Assessment Certification or other relevant certifications
- Workplace incident mitigation or de-escalation and business continuity planning experience
- Proficient in Microsoft Office; including use of Excel pivot tables and development of charts/graphics

title: Account Representative Intern, Early Career - 2027
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.
You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.


Key job responsibilities
Work backwards from the customer, identifying inputs to grow brands and improve their performance across Amazon's retail categories.

Support vendor managers and cross-functional teams — including in-stock, marketing, and category teams — to deliver business growth.

Build an understanding of customer pain points, requirements, and potential value that can be delivered through retail, advertising, or merchant services.

Identify target accounts using market data and industry intelligence, and learn the advertising or merchant services portfolio.

Collect, analyse, and review data to develop analytical and problem-solving skills, uncovering insights that drive business improvement.

Identify opportunities to improve products, services, processes, systems, and tools across the business.

Work with product teams and technical support teams to implement improvement projects.

A day in the life

Depending on your team, you might be supporting a vendor manager to grow a strategic brand within a retail category, helping account managers create compelling advertising presentations for clients, or driving new business growth across Amazon's third-party merchants. You might spend your morning analysing market data and customer insights to identify target accounts and growth opportunities, then spend your afternoon working with category or product teams to implement an improvement project.

Amazon is a customer-obsessed business, so no matter which team you join, part of your role will involve working backwards from the customer to understand their pain points and deliver value. You'll gain a deep understanding of Amazon's e-commerce retail business, advertising products, or merchant services portfolio, and partner across functions to deliver results — building your analytical, commercial, and stakeholder management skills in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

At Amazon Marketplace, we take pride in enabling all our Selling Partners to be successful – whether they’re a small business or a global corporation. We provide durable solutions to promote their products and increase their sales through a great shopping experience.

You'll collaborate with interns from around the world, networking and participating in social events to broaden your perspectives. You can also join specialized groups focused on areas like sustainability to explore your diverse interests.

Support:
The internship program provides a robust support system, including weekly intern office hours, dedicated IT and HR support, and a program team committed to your success. This ensures you have the guidance and assistance needed to thrive.

Learning Sessions:
Exclusive learning sessions will further enhance your skills, granting you access to Amazon's industry-leading learning platforms and the expertise of industry leaders. These structured development opportunities will prepare you for the next step in your career.

Opportunities:
Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.

Internship Start Dates across the year:
We are hiring interns to start anytime from January through September 2027. Each month, we'll hold 1-2 onboarding days for new hires.

- Currently in your final year and working towards a university bachelor’s or master’s in Engineering, Commerce, Business administration or similar field

Preferred qualifications

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to identify process improvements and innovative solutions.
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills, able to collaborate effectively with others.

title: Display Compliance Manager, Regulatory Intelligence, Safety, and Compliance (RISC)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking an experienced compliance professional with regulatory expertise in product safety and consumer protection to serve as a Display Compliance Program Manager. In this role you will drive the implementation and quality of mandatory compliance information displays across Amazon's EU and international storefronts, ensuring customers see accurate, well-placed regulatory information throughout their shopping journey.

The successful candidate will work across regulatory program teams, legal, engineering, and business stakeholders to define display requirements, drive implementation roadmaps, and coordinate delivery of compliant display solutions across product detail pages, checkout, search, and advertising surfaces. The Program Manager will navigate complex regulatory landscapes across multiple EU jurisdictions, manage competing priorities from domain programs, and partner closely with technical teams to deliver compliant display solutions at scale. This role will also engage externally with regulatory bodies and support responses to regulatory inquiries and enforcement actions.

Key job responsibilities
• Define display compliance requirements for EU and international regulatory frameworks (e.g., product safety, energy labeling, food information, radio equipment, packaging/takeback, chemical labeling), translating legal obligations into clear functional requirements for engineering teams.

• Own the end-to-end display implementation roadmap: intake regulatory requirements, scope and prioritize displays, coordinate cross-functional delivery with engineering teams, and drive launch readiness across multiple marketplaces.

• Actively contribute to technical delivery processes — participating in requirements documentation, user acceptance testing, and technical design discussions — ensuring compliance requirements are accurately reflected in implementation.

• Maintain a horizon view of evolving EU regulatory requirements to detect and respond to new display obligations; proactively scope and sequence implementation to prevent reactive escalations.

• Drive cross-functional coordination between regulatory program teams, legal, engineering, and business stakeholders to resolve implementation blockers, negotiate timelines, and align competing priorities across multiple concurrent workstreams.

• Manage regulatory escalations and enforcement responses related to display compliance gaps — including authority inquiries, potential fines, and high-severity incidents — ensuring timely resolution and clear stakeholder communication.

• Partner with quality assurance and data accuracy teams to define and maintain display quality standards, including placement accuracy, information accuracy, and format compliance.

• Enable display compliance for new shopping formats and surfaces by creating scalable onboarding frameworks and requirement mappings that can be reused across launches.

• Prepare reports and status communications to senior management with timely, actionable intelligence on display coverage metrics, quality gaps, regulatory risks, and program health.

• Identify and implement Generative AI solutions to scale compliance monitoring, improve detection capabilities, and streamline regulatory workflows while ensuring responsible AI use aligned with internal policies.

About the team
The Display Compliance team sits within Amazon's regulatory compliance organization for EU and international stores, protecting customers, brands, and selling partners by ensuring mandatory product compliance information is accurately and prominently displayed across all customer-facing surfaces. The program owns the "last mile" of regulatory information delivery — translating complex EU directives into visible, accurate, well-placed compliance displays that build customer trust while enabling business growth at scale. The team operates at the intersection of regulation, technology, and customer experience, managing display implementations across 15+ marketplaces, coordinating with multiple engineering teams, and navigating regulatory requirements internationally.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience in compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent
- Experience handling confidential information

Preferred qualifications

- Professional auditing qualification, or similar risk or compliance credentials
- Experience with SQL and Excel
- Experience in program requirements definition, together with data and metrics leveraging to drive improvements

title: Data Center Controls Engineer
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center.  Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.

Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.

Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.

Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers.

Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management.

Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.

Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.

Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.

Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for a Regional Safety Manager to build and own the safety risk program for Amazon Cloud Logistics (ACL) across a global region. This is a newly created role where you will define the safety strategy for data center logistics operations, drive risk reduction across ACL activities, and serve as the single point of coordination between ACL and AWS Data Center Health and Safety (DCHS). You will manage multiple concurrent risk programs spanning incident reporting, root cause investigations, risk assessments, contractor safety, and inspection coordination — all while partnering with operations leaders, regional DCHS teams, and vendor organizations. If you are an experienced safety professional who is energized by building programs from scratch and influencing stakeholders across a complex, global organization, this role gives you the autonomy to shape how safety scales with one of the fastest-growing functions in AWS infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end incident reporting lifecycle for ACL operations across DCHS regions, define safety KPIs such as injury rates and leading indicators, and build dashboards that drive data-informed decisions at regional and global levels.
- Manage the root cause and corrective action program for ACL incidents, identify patterns across investigations, and recommend corrective actions that address systemic causes rather than symptoms.
- Review and approve Risk Assessments and Method Statements for ACL logistics activities — including rack deployment, liquid cooling delivery, and heavy equipment operations — and develop standardized handling guidance that scales globally with regional customization.
- Coordinate safety inspections at ACL operational sites, align protocols with DCHS standards, and design training programs that build safety capability across DCHS managers, operations leaders, and the ACL vendor workforce.
