title: Cost Estimator, Worldwide Grocery Stores - Growth & Development
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores, Growth & Development team is looking for a Cost Estimator to join our Store Development team.

Are you ready to play a critical financial role in one of the world's most ambitious physical retail expansions? In this role, your cost models and analysis will directly shape how Amazon builds hundreds of grocery stores across North America. You won't be tracking project budgets, you'll be building program-level cost baselines, driving portfolio analytics, and delivering the executive-level insights that help leadership make smarter investment decisions across a portfolio of 600+ locations.

Here's what makes this role different:
- You work at the program level, not the project level. Your job is to understand what it costs to build a store, why those costs shift, and how to keep our financial models current, contributing directly to how leadership makes smarter financial decisions at scale.
- Your work reaches the top. The baselines you build and the analyses you run feed directly into senior leadership conversations, monthly executive reports, and financial planning for the broader organization.
- You'll be a true cross-functional connector. You'll work closely with design, construction, finance, capital planning, and procurement teams, engaging directly with general contractors and external consultants, connecting you to some of the most important work in the business.
- You'll contribute to shaping the tools, not just use them. You'll provide input on the AI-powered analytics platforms and construction management systems our team relies on, supporting process improvements and governance that help the whole organization run more efficiently.
- You'll make the whole operation smarter over time. Every project you close out, every driver you identify, and every lesson learned feeds back into sharper baselines and better assumptions, so the next store format or new market benefits from everything we've already built.

If you're energized by the idea of bringing financial rigor to a fast-moving, large-scale retail operation, you have construction experience, and you want your work to compound in impact as the portfolio grows, this is the role for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Build and maintain program-level cost baselines across store formats and retail concepts, keeping financial models current as market conditions and construction costs evolve
- Execute portfolio-wide budget variance analyses and reconcile actual spend against planned baselines, covering both active and completed projects
- Support proforma updates as cost drivers shift, and collaborate with design, construction, capital planning, and procurement partners on trade-offs that impact financial goals
- Prepare monthly and quarterly cost performance data and supporting analyses for leadership review, contributing to executive review meetings and coordinating follow-up items
- Engage directly with general contractors and external consultants to gather cost data, validate assumptions, and support governance and cost validation processes
- Support process improvement, governance, and controls within construction management systems to improve data quality, consistency, and operational efficiency at portfolio scale
- Contribute to the team's AI and analytics strategy by gathering requirements, supporting tool adoption, and tracking the impact of new platform implementations
- Apply lessons learned from completed projects to continuously sharpen cost baseline assumptions and inform cost models for new store formats and capital programs

A day in the life
Most of your time centers on keeping cost models and financial baselines sharp: analyzing why costs are shifting, costing out new initiatives/formats, and making sure the right data is ready before big decisions get made. On any given day, you might be on a call with a general contractor validating cost assumptions, or working through how a design change affects an overall program cost. What you learn from each closed project feeds directly back into sharper models for the next store format. Beyond the routine, expect rapid executive requests, new concept launches, and engagement across the entire organization.

About the team
The Cost Management team is the financial accountability and controllership engine of our Store Development organization. We own the cost intelligence, vendor performance, and financial governance programs that help leadership invest smarter and operate more efficiently across 600+ grocery locations. We are a direct execution team: we do not advise on problems. We own and solve them. Every program we run is designed to scale with the business. If you join this team, you will be expected to execute with precision, build with rigor, and make the work better than you found it.

- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- Experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's project management representative or in other Commercial Development and Construction related disciplines
- Experience with advanced use of Excel and using statistical analysis applications, or experience in construction or project management
- Experience in financial modeling, or experience with data analytics platforms (Power BI, Python, SQL, Tableau)
- Experience working with General Contractors and construction consultants on cost-related deliverables
- 5+ years of experience in cost management, financial analysis, or construction cost management

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in retail or grocery construction projects
- Familiarity with construction cost indices (e.g., CCI) and industry benchmarking methodologies
- Experience supporting external consultant relationships in a construction or real estate development context
- Track record of contributing to cost reduction strategies

title: Sr. Worldwide Specialist - Signal Activation , Data & AI GTM
descriptionHtml:
Are you excited about turning signal into action at scale? We are looking for a Senior Data & AI GTM Specialist to build and own the campaign execution arm that activates the AWS field the moment we detect a meaningful signal. Today our team synthesizes field, customer, and product signals into structured go-to-market recommendations. This role extends that capability by owning what happens next, converting a detected signal into a targeted, sequenced campaign that reaches the right field teams and the right customers within minutes to days rather than weeks or months.

Signals come from everywhere. Internally, they surface through seller conversations, deal blockers, product feature requests, , opportunity and pipeline data, and win and loss patterns. Externally, they surface through competitive moves, model launches, customer forum activity, and industry trends. Your job is to make sure that when a signal crosses a threshold worth acting on, a well-designed campaign fires automatically or near-automatically, with differentiated asks grounded in each account's context.

This is not traditional business development where you manage a handful of named accounts. Instead, you will design the mechanism that listens for signal, decides which signals warrant field activation, and orchestrates the outreach, enablement, and follow-through that turns that activation into pipeline. You will build this on top of our existing signal synthesis program and increasingly leverage agentic AI to move from manual triage toward an always-on detect-and-activate loop. You will own the full path from signal to seller action to measurable pipeline outcome.

You will be a deep expert in using AI to derive signal from noise and in using AI to execute on that signal at scale. This is the defining technical skill of the role. You will apply AI both to mine thousands of internal and external inputs for the patterns that matter and to turn those patterns into field activation faster and more precisely than any manual process could.

Key job responsibilities
Own the signal-to-activation mechanism end to end, defining which internal and external signals warrant field activations, campaigns, asset updates, or knowledge base improvements, and the closed-loop tracking that confirms the field acted and the signal was resolved

Design and launch targeted activation campaigns that convert a detected signal into a differentiated, sequenced field ask, reaching the right sellers and customers with context-aware messaging rather than undifferentiated broadcast

Build on the existing GTM signal synthesis capability, extending it from insight generation into campaign execution so that structured recommendations translate directly into field motion

Establish differentiated, cohort-based targeting that segments accounts by journey stage, existing pipeline, and prior actions, ensuring each seller receives an ask proportional to where their account already is

Ingest and normalize signal from diverse sources, including seller conversations, internal AI assistant prompts, deal blockers, product feature requests, opportunity data, competitive intelligence, model launches, and customer forums

Be a deep expert in using AI to derive signal and to execute on signal at scale, applying AI both to mine thousands of internal and external inputs for the patterns that matter and to convert those patterns into precise field activation faster than any manual process

Operate agentic AI mechanisms that mine signal in real time, prioritize what matters, and increasingly auto-generate the activation and recommendation, moving the team from manual triage toward an always-on loop

Drive internal teams to build and maintain the signal architecture, holding the source teams accountable for the pipelines, instrumentation, and data quality that keep signal flowing reliably from every internal and external source

Partner with Finance and Sales Operations to surface the top signals that are stalling deals in business reviews, quantifying blocked pipeline by root cause and turning that view into prioritized field action

Partner cross-functionally with the signal synthesis owner, product and service GTM teams, demand marketing, field enablement, sales leadership, and analytics to align activation campaigns to product priorities and field capacity

Define the business requirements for reporting that quantifies activation impact and blocked pipeline by root cause, giving leadership visibility into what signals drove which outcomes

Measure, report, and optimize activation campaigns against pipeline generated, conversion rate, deal velocity, signal resolution time, and revenue influence, presenting results to senior leadership

Continuously improve the mechanism, running experiments on signal thresholds, targeting logic, messaging, and channels so activation gets sharper and faster over time

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing the overnight signal queue. Your AI mining mechanism has flagged a spike in field conversations and internal AI assistant prompts referencing a competitor's new product launch. You assess whether it clears the threshold for a field activation, confirm it does, and begin shaping the campaign. You define the target cohort using existing account intelligence, so that sellers already engaged on the topic get a lighter validate-and-advance ask while sellers with no engagement get the full play.

Mid-morning, you meet with Finance and Sales Operations to review the top deal blockers stalling pipeline this month. You work through which blockers trace back to product gaps, unlaunched models, or competitive pressure, quantify the blocked pipeline behind each, and decide which ones warrant a field activation or an escalation to the owning product team. You also spend time with the internal teams that own the upstream signal sources, holding them accountable for the instrumentation and data quality that keep signal flowing reliably.

After lunch, you work with the product GTM lead for a service approaching a major milestone. You align on positioning and which customer segments to prioritize, then wire the launch into your activation mechanism so that the moment the signal goes live, the field receives a coordinated ask rather than a scattered one. You also review how your agentic mining agent performed on last week's signals, tuning its prioritization so the highest-value patterns rise to the top automatically.

Later in the afternoon, you pull together a metrics read-out for leadership. You show pipeline influenced by activation, signal resolution time, and how differentiated targeting is outperforming broadcast on both engagement and deal size. You call out one activation exceeding targets and recommend scaling it, and you flag a signal source that is generating noise rather than value and propose refining its threshold.

Before wrapping up, you spend time in the field channels where sellers are responding to your latest activation. A few surface customer stories and blockers worth capturing. You feed those back into the mechanism to sharpen the next activation and to ensure each blocker gets a tracked response, closing the loop between what the field told us and what we did about it.

About the team
We are the Data & AI GTM Acceleration team within Amazon Web Services. Our mission is to help every AWS customer realize the value of AI and data services faster. We build and operate go-to-market programs and initiatives that connect the right customer with the right solution at the right moment, at a scale that a traditional sales model cannot reach on its own.

We sit at the center of a broad ecosystem. On one side, we work with AWS product and GTM teams building AI and data services. On the other, we partner with thousands of field sellers, solution architects, and inside sales professionals who bring those services to customers. Our job is to bridge the gap between what the field is telling us and what the field does next, turning signal into coordinated action.

What makes this team unique is how we operate. We build, we prove, and we scale. We prototype new go-to-market mechanisms, validate them with real sellers and real customers, and then hand proven playbooks to enterprise scaling partners who deploy them across the global AWS field. We move quickly, experiment often, and measure everything. We are increasingly AI-native in how we work, building and operating agents that mine field signal and deliver personalized recommendations directly into seller workflows.

Culturally, we are builders obsessed with measurable impact. We operate with a high degree of autonomy, trust each other to own outcomes end to end, and maintain a bias for action even when the path forward is not fully defined. You will work alongside people who are curious, technically fluent, collaborative across organizational boundaries, and energized by the pace of change in AI.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. title: Software Development Engineer II, Lightsail
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Lightsail makes AWS accessible to developers and business customers who want to get their cloud stacks running in seconds without the complexity of traditional infrastructure. As a Software Development Engineer II on the Lightsail team, you will build features and services that simplify compute, storage, networking, and website hosting for customers who need things to just work. The team is expanding quickly, adding new capabilities like website hosting and agent hosting, and you will help shape what comes next. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, from understanding customer problems through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operations. If you are an engineer who enjoys building products you would actually use yourself, and you want to do that at AWS scale, we would like to talk to you.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build features for Amazon Lightsail's distributed systems, working in Java, Go, JavaScript, and React across both backend services and frontend experiences.
- Collaborate with partner teams across AWS — including Amazon EC2, Amazon Route 53, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) — to integrate Lightsail capabilities with the broader AWS ecosystem.
- Own the operational health of the services you build by identifying root causes of production issues and driving permanent fixes, ensuring customers experience reliable performance.
- Participate actively in design reviews and code reviews, providing constructive feedback to teammates and mentoring other engineers on writing clean, maintainable code.
- Evaluate new technologies and approaches, including generative artificial intelligence tools, to improve team productivity and the quality of solutions delivered to customers.

A day in the life
You start your morning checking operational dashboards for a Lightsail service you recently launched, then join a design review where you and a teammate work through how to integrate a new hosting capability with an existing AWS service. After lunch, you pick up a feature task, writing backend logic in Java and wiring up the React console so customers can try it out. Later, you review a pull request from a teammate, leave detailed feedback, and update documentation so the next engineer who touches this code can ramp up quickly.

About the team
Amazon Lightsail sits within AWS and has a distinctive mission: make cloud infrastructure simple and approachable for non-enterprise customers. While we run on the same AWS infrastructure that powers the world's largest workloads, our focus is on removing complexity so developers and small businesses can launch and scale without a steep learning curve. We are an inclusive team that values knowledge sharing and mentorship, and we intentionally assign projects to help each engineer grow. Right now we are investing in new hosting and agent capabilities, so there is plenty of room to have a direct impact on what we build next.

- 2+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. We're seeking a dedicated Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) Manager to join our mission of creating the world's safest work environment. This role offers an exciting opportunity to directly impact associate well being while driving operational excellence.

As a WHS Manager, you'll be the site's safety champion, leading our Global WHS Program implementation. You'll combine hands-on safety management with strategic thinking to protect our most valuable asset – our people. Your role bridges the gap between safety requirements and operational success, requiring both technical expertise and strong interpersonal skills. Working closely with Operations leadership, you'll drive safety initiatives that make a real difference. You'll conduct comprehensive risk assessments, analyze safety data, and implement practical solutions that protect associates while supporting productivity. Your ability to build relationships and influence positive change will be essential as you help shape our safety culture. You'll lead safety compliance efforts, conduct thorough site audits, and analyze incident trends to target improvements where they matter most. Managing our first aid program and emergency response capabilities, you'll ensure immediate care is always available. Your analytical skills will transform safety data into actionable insights, while your leadership abilities will help engage associates in our safety mission.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Leadership & Innovation - Transform safety culture through leadership and innovative solutions. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that set new benchmarks in workplace safety. Leverage technology and data analytics to drive preventive safety measures that protect our associates while enhancing operational excellence. Develop leadership plans, communicate expectations, and drive initiatives to create a safe work environment. Measure performance against WHS policies, analyze metrics, and conduct site audits to address non-compliance issues.

Strategic Partnership & Influence - Build partnerships with Operations leadership to integrate safety into every aspect of our business. Use compelling data analysis and risk insights to influence positive change and drive strategic decision-making. Establish yourself as a trusted advisor who balances safety excellence with operational demands. Oversee recordkeeping, workplace organization, and WHS training programs.

- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach

- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- 3+ years of increasing responsibilities in WHS and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations
- 3+ years of increasing responsibilities in people and performance management, or 2+ years of Amazon Safety (blue badge/FTE) experience

Preferred qualifications

- Distribution Center or Manufacturing EHS experience with mix of exempt and non-exempt employees at a site of at least 250 people
- Master’s degree
- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment.
- Experience in a fast paced, dynamic organization
- Certified Safety Professional
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interfacing with site leader
- Ability to develop and implement department goals and strategies
- Strong analytical skills with demonstrated problem solving ability

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Devices – the team behind the best-selling Amazon Echo, Alexa, Kindle E-reader, Fire Tablet, Fire TV, Cloud Cam and Dash Button product lines—is seeking a seasoned product manager to join the Devices Pricing and Promotions team to help lead our pricing strategy and systems.

Our organization’s vision is to use science to automate forecasting, allocation, marketing, pricing and purchasing decisions for the Devices business. We build science and technology to create Hands Off the Wheel systems that automate digital marketing planning, creating operating and financial efficiencies for Amazon Devices. We are an interdisciplinary team that combines the talents of science and engineering to develop and deliver solutions that measurably achieve this goal.

We are looking for an experienced Sr Product Manager - Technical to tackle complex and ambiguous marketing optimization and automation problems that span numerous systems and organizations across the Devices business (Echo Device Family, FireTV, eReaders, Tablets etc.). They will be a highly visible individual that will own the communication, coordination, and execution of a long-term, multi-year product vision. As a Sr. Product Manager over our marketing planning workflow tools, you’ll partner with our team of research scientists, data scientists, economists, and developers to build out the next generation of marketing optimization and automation.



Key job responsibilities
As an ideal candidate, you have a passion to understand the interplay of our different marketing strategies to fuel scale and automation. You are responsible for defining and driving our product roadmaps. You will work with product line teams, forecasting teams, in-house scientists, data-engineers, economists, software teams, and product line marketers to identify new features and projects. As a product strategist, you must analyze the potential customer and financial implications, select the most promising ideas, prioritize them and create a cohesive roadmap. You will also evangelize new features to our internal customers, working to accelerate their adoption, track the impacts, and communicate results with senior leaders.

This is a highly visible position. You must have the experience and capability to prepare documentation for senior executives and align your roadmap with Devices strategic objectives. Excellent written, verbal communication and data analytical skills are a necessity. Successful candidates should thrive in a highly collaborative, creative, analytical, and fast-paced environment oriented around delivering better prices to customers worldwide. You will excel at looking around corners, and anticipating where to build and when to test to fail fast.

A day in the life
• Define the multi-year vision for the space
• Build and manage high quality product roadmaps based on your vision and strategy
• Work backwards to determine what the initial building blocks to achieve that vision will be
• Work with key business stakeholders, engineering partner teams, Pricing Research, and Central Econ to build out requirements for the different phases
• Work with our in-house engineering team to build and innovate in the space
• Manage prioritization and trade-offs for speed to launch, performance, and features
• Gain support for your strategy and roadmap from stakeholders by writing narratives and influencing peers and senior leadership
Creating program goals and related metrics, track progress and manage through obstacles to achieve your objectives
• Drive adoption of pricing science across organization with key stakeholders, including product line teams and functional partner teams.

- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 6, 2026

In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The HR Partner role offers an exceptional opportunity to build your career in human resources, focusing on employee experience, engagement, leadership development and HR operational excellence.

As an HR Partner on the NASC PXT team, you will support PXT operations through consistent standard work execution, relationship-building, and timely issue resolution. With a visible presence across site operations, you'll foster team culture, support engagement, and coach leaders on PXT practices. You'll create positive employee experiences while building your skills in navigating increasingly complex issues and influencing without authority. Success in this role comes from building strong partnerships, demonstrating sound judgment, and maintaining a customer-centric approach. You'll learn to use data-driven insights and HR technologies to enhance the employee experience while developing core HR capabilities that will serve as the foundation for your career growth.

You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility.

Key job responsibilities
- Support a positive employee experience by executing key programs, reinforcing workplace standards, and partnering with PXT and Operations to create a culture where employees feel valued, heard, and supported.

- Execute standard work with consistent quality and timeliness, meeting established service level agreements (SLAs) and maintaining accurate documentation of HR processes and employee interactions.

- Provide frontline employee support by responding to inquiries, addressing concerns, and ensuring appropriate resolution or escalation of employee matters. Handle sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.

- Assist in running and monitoring feedback channels such as roundtables, floor walks, and employee engagement activities. Support issue tracking and follow-up, partnering with senior PXT team members to drive resolutions and improvements in employee experience.

- Coach frontline leaders on behaviors that impact engagement and retention. Reinforce expectations and guide leaders in selecting and effectively utilizing available tools to improve team communication, recognition, and performance conversations.

- Support the execution of site-level engagement, communication, and culture-building initiatives. Coordinate logistics, gather feedback, and monitor effectiveness.

- Learn to track and summarize PXT-related data (e.g., attrition/attendance trends, hiring data, employee sentiment). Help prepare insights for site reviews or team discussions.

- Promote the use of self-service tools to resolve routine employee and manager questions. Help identify recurring gaps and escalate opportunities to improve tool usability or adoption.

A day in the life
A typical day involves balancing standard work execution with responsive employee support. You'll maintain consistent presence on the operations floor, engaging directly with hourly employees and partnering with leaders to address concerns and drive engagement initiatives. Operating under the guidance of senior team members, you'll execute core HR processes while ensuring quality service delivery.

Through data tools and HR technologies, you'll assist in tracking metrics and identifying trends, while developing your ability to build trust through personal interaction. You'll support employee engagement activities, help coordinate feedback channels, and assist in coaching and development of others. When complex issues arise, you'll seek guidance from senior team members, learning to navigate challenging situations while developing sound judgment.

Success in this role comes from maintaining organized routines, demonstrating strong follow-through, and building effective partnerships with both the PXT team and operations leaders. descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

We’re looking for people who innovate and love solving hard problems and building hardware. You will work hard, have fun, and make history!

Key job responsibilities
Perform structural/dynamic loads analyses, and multi-body dynamic simulations for subsystem and vehicle level trades.
Contribute to spacecraft structural/dynamics test planning, equipment and instrumentation selection, and data acquisition.
Perform analysis using FEA models for all vehicle states: GSE/transport, launch vehicle (stowed), on-orbit states (dispensing, deployments).
Pretest simulations, response limiting/notching definition, and post-test data analysis and correlation/validation of analytical model.
Work with GNC team to deliver linear modal models of principal structural disturbance responses to the integrated flight simulation & similar analysis tools.
Verify compliance with launch vehicle requirements

A day in the life
Loads and Dynamics engineers are responsible for spacecraft level loads analyses across the entire spacecraft life cycle (concept and configuration development, design, test, validation, qualification, and in-service operations). Our engineers work closely with many other technical disciplines and organizations to integrate solutions to complex engineering problems and have both large impact and high visibility.

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience
- 6+ years of experience in dynamic analysis and testing (modal, random vibration, impact, shock, and/or acoustics)
- 6+ years experience with finite element analysis NASTRAN (or equivalent)

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent
- 6+ years of experience with model preparation delivery and interpretation of results for coupled load analysis, including experience with component modal synthesis reduction techniques, such as Craig-Bampton
- 6+ years of experience in on orbit disturbance modeling and multi-body dynamics
- 6+ years of experience with modal testing and correlation of hardware
- Demonstrated experience in several of the following areas: full vehicle qualification, component testing, dynamic analysis with MSC ADAMS/Wave6/LS-DYNA, MATLAB/PYTHON programming, and experience with FEMAP/IMAT

title: Logistics Specialist L3, AWS Logistics Services
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Logistics Specialists play a vital role in the success of Amazon Web Services by providing the right part, in the right place at the right time. Your contribution to this success would be maintaining the onsite parts room in AWS Data Centers, by managing the custody of computer hardware through their entire lifecycle. This involves receiving parts, safely storing parts, picking and delivering parts to hardware technicians, cycle counts, and shipping faulty hardware back to the vendor.

You will work closely with Data Centre Operations and Engineering teams to ensure reliable functioning and repair activities to support our customers, while adhering to our operational tenants of safety, security and availability.

Key job responsibilities
- Maintaining inventory to ensure that proper stock levels are managed to support build and repair activities.
- Physically receiving and issuing out of parts as needed for internal customers.
- Loading, unloading and transporting parts between different sites.
- Keeping accurate stock records for all items within our care through physical cycle counts.
- Maintaining the safety, organization, and cleanliness of all workspaces using Amazon 7S principles
Travel:
- The role may require the successful candidate to travel to other sites in the in the Melbourne metro area to assist in conducting cycle counts, receiving stock into the inventory control system, replenishing stock and returning defective stock. Travel between sites will require own transport, all travel related costs will be reimbursed.

Physical / Environmental Demands:
- Amazon Operates with a principle of safety first. With this principle, we take significant care to ensure all employees operate in a safe manner and have appropriate tools to support them in undertaking their roles safely. The activities below are required with the safety principle applied.
- Loading and unloading shipments.
- Standing, sitting, and walking (including stairs) for prolonged periods of time.
- Willing and able to frequently push, pull, squat, bend and kneel.
- Reach and stretch to position equipment and fixtures while maintaining balance.
- Push or pull heavy objects of up to 16kg into position and participate in group lifts of 20kg or more.
- Coordinate body movements when using tools or equipment.
- Work with and/or around moving mechanical parts.
- Work in an office and warehouse environment where the noise level is low to moderate.

A day in the life
The MEL Data Center Logistics team, supports infrastructure deployment across Melbourne's data center cluster. We manage the end-to-end logistics lifecycle — receiving, ingesting, inventory management, and cycle count accuracy — ensuring critical components are available to keep builds on track. Our culture is built on ownership, continuous learning, and bias for action. We've developed a structured training program that accelerates on boarding and equips new members to contribute quickly. Operating across multiple MEL sites, we embrace start-up challenges as opportunities to build scalable processes. Our work directly enables AWS to serve millions of customers worldwide.

Your day will be spent carrying out Logistical support functions for our Data Centers. This will involve physical control and processing of spare parts transactions, consumables stock replenishment, and cycle counting of stock.

A day in the life
Du betreust ein Instandhaltungsteam innerhalb einer Schicht und sorgst dafür, dass alle Mitarbeitenden die erforderlichen Werkzeuge zur Verfügung haben und diese einwandfrei funktionieren. Das beinhaltet die Überwachung von Prozessen, damit Vorschriften und Richtlinien befolgt werden, ebenso wie die Gewährleistung der Durchführung vorbeugender Wartungsmaßnahmen, um die Betriebszeit unserer Anlagen zu maximieren.
Durch Deine Beobachtungen während der Schichtarbeit machst Du Verbesserungsvorschläge, um unsere Systeme noch effizienter und produktiver zu gestalten, und setzt diese Verbesserungen EU-weit um. Außerdem nutzt Du Tools wie SCADA zur Überwachung von Prozessen, um deren Leistungsfähigkeit zu gewährleisten, und unterstützt administrative Aufgaben in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Deinen Führungskräften.
Du arbeitest vor Ort in einem unserer Logistikzentren. Du arbeitest in Schichtmodellen, die Nächte und Wochenenden umfassen können. Mit den Kenntnissen und Erfahrungen, die Du sammelst, wirst Du Dich zu weiteren Führungspositionen weiterentwickeln.

About the team
Unser Wartungs- und Instandhaltungsteam (Reliability Maintenance Engineering Team oder RME-Team) sorgt dafür, dass unsere Geräte und Ausstattung jederzeit optimal funktionieren. Wir sind ein Team von Techniker:innen und Ingenieur:innen, das aus hervorragenden Teamplayern besteht und von erfahrenen Führungskräften geleitet wird. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam daran, die Geräte in unserem gesamten globalen Netzwerk von Fulfillment-Centern zu warten, zu reparieren und ihre Fehler zu beheben. Einige unserer Mitarbeiter:innen sind Führungskräfte, die das Team bei der Arbeit an spannender, innovativer Technologie beaufsichtigen – die es teilweise nur bei Amazon gibt.
Von der Installation automatisierter Verpackungssysteme bis hin zur Beaufsichtigung der allgemeinen Wartungsarbeiten eines Standorts sowie der Reparatur von für den Vertrieb wesentlichen Geräten wickelt unser Team einen Großteil der technischen Aufgaben bei Amazon ab. Unter anderem sorgt es auch dafür, dass Gebäude weiterhin den rechtlichen Auflagen entsprechen, damit alle sicher bleiben und unsere Standorte mit maximaler Effizienz betrieben werden. Es gibt zahlreiche Aufstiegschancen im RME-Team selbst ebenso wie im gesamten Amazon-Unternehmen.
Alle unsere Aktivitäten sind darauf ausgerichtet, die Ausfallzeiten an Amazons wichtigsten Betriebsstandorten zu reduzieren, damit Kund:innen ihre Bestellungen rechtzeitig erhalten. Oft arbeiten wir früh morgens, spät abends oder in der Nachtschicht, um Wartungsarbeiten mit den geringstmöglichen Störungen vorzunehmen. Falls wir eine bessere Möglichkeit finden, eine bestimmte Aufgabe zu erledigen, verfügen wir über die Fertigkeiten und Gelegenheiten, vollständig neue Prozesse oder bahnbrechende Technologie wie Amazon Robotics oder unseren Complex Item Sorter einzuführen.

Sc., MA, M. Sc., Dipl.-Ing.)

title: Data Centre Operations Manager, Data Center Operations
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.


Key job responsibilities
About You:
You will have previous management experience, managing teams of high performers.
You will have the ability to refine and develop processes to optimise operational excellence in every area of your role.
You will be able to drive performance levels to achieve the pace we build and operate our Data Centres.
You will have previous experience in Data Centres, either building or managing (or both) along with exposure to developing great relationships with both internal teams and external vendors.

You will also have a passion for technology along with a desire to be the best at your job every day!

About The Role:
As a Data Center Manager in Amazon Web Services AWS, you will get to manage the world’s largest Cloud Computing Infrastructure. We encounter interesting, challenging & complex problems every day, being a technical manager in AWS means that you can innovate to solve these issues and help drive Operations Excellence in all areas of your role.

A day in the life

Your day job will include (but not limited to):

Managing and developing teams of engineers, providing both technical and leadership expertise and ensuring highest levels of performance.
Maintaining existing co-located and in-house Data Centres
Helping build and bring online new Data Centres
Constantly improving all our processes and procedures. We believe there is nothing we cannot improve
Assisting & managing relationships with external vendors & contractors
Liaising with internal teams & management groups
Ensuring we adhere to and exceed local Health & Safety standards in all our Data Centres
Creating and maintaining metrics on all aspects of our Data Centres and utilising those metrics to drive positive changes
Assisting in implementing service methodologies including incident management, problem management, change management, capacity management, etc.

What are we looking for in a successful AWS Data Centre Manager (DCM) candidate along with the technical knowledge and experience?

People Management.
As a successful candidate you will have managed a team of at least 5 individuals, over a period of at least 3 years. You will be able to demonstrate how you have continued to improve performance of an existing team along with displaying skills in creating or growing a team. Experience managing both high & low performing employees will be of advantage along with conflict management.

Incident Management.
You will have a lot of experience dealing with high severity situations, show a clear understanding of the wider blast implications of any issue/outage and potential consequences of differing outcome scenarios. You will also have experience in Change Management & Fault Management.

Vendor Management.
An Amazon, the DCM has to deal with vendors, contractors & security companies. You will be able to prove you have experience dealing with partners and be able to display incidents of both problem & conflict management when dealing with same.

Process Improvement.
You will be able to demonstrate an ability of taking both a good working process & a bad process and improving. You will have experience in processes mapping, implementing remediation steps and how this affected the overall business you were working in. Experience in Kaizen/Lean/Six Sigma is preferable

Health & Safety.
Health & Safety should be at the forefront of every DCMs mind. Managers should be able to positively influence the Safety culture of the Data Centre organization.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

- Experience with computer hardware troubleshooting and repair
- Experience in data center engineering or operations
- Experience in people management and team development
- Experience managing complex and fast-moving issues
- Experience analyzing metrics to drive business improvements

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Six Sigma tools and Lean techniques
- Experience collecting, analyzing, and utilizing data to drive process and system improvements

descriptionHtml:
About Amazon

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. If you'd like to help us build the place to find and buy anything online, this is your chance to make history by joining the North American Operations recruiting team at Amazon.

It's a contractual role.
Locations: Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, and Gurgaon (Remote role)
Timing: 6:00 PM - 3:00 AM IST

Role Overview
We need an exceptionally talented Sourcer Recruiter to help us find the best talent in the US market to support our growth. Amazon is one of the most recognizable brand names in the world and we distribute millions of products each year to our loyal customers. The Recruiter will work with a team of recruiting professionals focusing on finding the best distribution and operations professionals across the country, fostering a collaborative team environment and a strong service-oriented culture that ensures delivery of efficient, effective, quality-driven service to internal customers.

Key Requirements
The candidate must be able to successfully manage, prioritize and close searches against a timeline and have experience setting benchmarks, metrics, and understand how to prioritize to hit all customer SLAs. They thrive in an innovative, fast-paced environment, can roll up their sleeves, work hard, have fun, and get the job done. The best candidates will have a reputation for being exceptional at candidate generation in a high volume environment and possess strong verbal and written communication skills. They will need to demonstrate an ability to prioritize their time, demonstrate pushback and a sense of urgency, and understand the value of providing amazing customer service.

Core Responsibilities
Recruit passive candidates with the mentality to "profile people and gauge chemistry of candidates for fit and understand their motivation" rather than sell a role
Build and maintain network of potential candidates through proactive market research and ongoing relationship management
Conduct in-depth interviews of potential candidates, demonstrating ability to anticipate hiring manager preferences through high offer-to-interview ratios
Recommend ideas and strategies related to recruitment that will contribute to the long-range growth of the company
Implement new processes and fine-tune standard processes for recruiting that fits within Amazon's mission to deliver the highest quality results to the customer

title: Learning Specialist, EU E2E Learning, Central Programs
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to shape how hundreds of people learn, grow, and do their best work? As our Learning Specialist, you won't just build training, you'll own the strategy behind it: designing, governing, and optimizing the learning ecosystem across multiple functions, solving real business problems, and designing learning that scales across teams and countries.

This is a role for someone who loves both the creative side of learning and the rigor of getting things done. You'll independently lead complex learning programs from idea to launch, design scalable solutions to problems where the answer isn't obvious yet, and partner with senior leaders to turn business priorities into learning that actually moves the needle. You'll set the "what" and the "how" that our Learning Coordinators bring to life, and you'll raise the bar on our methodology and standards along the way.

If you're energized by continuous improvement, comfortable managing multiple projects at once, and motivated by seeing measurable capability lift across an organization, you'll thrive here. You'll join a team that cares deeply about the learner experience, champions innovation, and gives you the autonomy to make a real, lasting impact.

Beyond the day-to-day, there's plenty of room to stretch. You might pilot how AI can transform the way we design and deliver learning, represent the team in cross-European initiatives, take the lead on org-wide programs, or mentor and shape the next generation of learning talent. If you bring the curiosity and the drive, this role will keep giving you bigger problems to solve.

Key job responsibilities
KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Learning Design & Program Management
- Own the full ADDIE lifecycle for assigned functions, designing solutions that scale across multiple teams and delivering high-quality training content.
- Apply expertise in adult learning theories and instructional design to solve complex learning problems where the problem is understood but the solution is not.
- Design and implement innovative learning solutions across multiple modalities (digital, classroom, experiential, self-paced, blended).
- Plan, launch, and manage end-to-end learning programs, owning scope, timelines, milestones, risks, and deliverables from concept to rollout.
- Manage multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities, keeping stakeholders informed with clear status, ETAs, and success metrics.
- Provide support and mentoring to Learning Coordinators across ES and UK.

Project Management & Delivery

- Lead learning projects using structured project management practices (planning, RACI, dependency and risk management, stakeholder communication, and delivery tracking).
- Maintain project governance mechanisms (trackers, dashboards, and reporting cadences) to ensure visibility and on-time delivery.
- Anticipate blockers and dependencies, build contingency plans, and drive projects to closure with clear owners and deadlines.

Continuous Improvement

- Apply continuous improvement methodologies to raise the quality and efficiency of learning programs and processes.
- Establish feedback loops (surveys, focus groups, defect and performance data) to systematically identify opportunities and implement improvement actions.
- Use data to prioritize improvements, define success metrics, and measure impact, driving measurable gains in learner experience and business outcomes.
- Standardize and document processes (SOPs, templates, reusable frameworks) to ensure sustainability and scalability.

Standards Ownership

- Own and evolve training standards, ensuring consistent quality across the learning ecosystem.
- Create engaging content that drives participant retention and knowledge application.
- Embed instructional design best practices and quality controls (e.g. Bloom's Taxonomy, Kirkpatrick evaluation) as the baseline for quality audits.

Stakeholder Partnership

- Act as the strategic learning partner to function leaders, translating business priorities into learning roadmaps.
- Partner with org-level stakeholders to secure resources, scope efforts, set priorities, and drive delivery.
- Work with partners across Europe to ensure alignment with best practices, processes, and technology.
- Lead change management for new programs and process changes, ensuring smooth adoption across teams.

Data-Driven Governance

- Define learning metrics and conduct Training Needs Analysis to identify knowledge gaps.
- Develop evaluation methods to measure training effectiveness and present insights and recommendations to leadership.
- Monitor program performance against targets, report trends, and translate data into action.

A day in the life
No two days look the same on the EU E2E Learning team, Central Programs, and that's part of the fun. One moment you're digging into program metrics, spotting a dip in a function's training scores and designing a scalable new module to close the gap; the next you're partnering with a function leader to turn a business priority into a learning roadmap. You'll mentor Learning Coordinators across ES and UK to bring your programs to life, jump between multiple projects, and get ahead of risks before they become blockers. AI is part of how you work every day: you'll use it to design content faster, analyze feedback and performance data for insights, evaluate learning objectives against business needs, and pilot new formats like interactive simulations and audio guides that make learning stick. Along the way you'll apply continuous improvement thinking to make the team a little faster and better every quarter, and you'll turn data into a clear story of impact for leadership. Some days you'll be deep in creative design work, others you'll be influencing senior stakeholders or championing how AI can transform the way our whole team learns and delivers. If you love that mix of creative design, strategic influence, hands-on delivery, and relentless improvement, this is the kind of day you'll look forward to.

About the team
The EU E2E Learning, Central Programs team is the learning and development engine for central functions across all three miles (first, middle, and last). We own the end-to-end learning journey, from Day 1 onboarding for new joiners through continuous development for tenured employees, so every person we support is ready to deliver from day one and keeps growing in their role. Alongside this, we set and evolve learning standards, audit standard operating procedures, and measure training effectiveness, all with a data-driven, continuous improvement mindset (increasingly powered by AI) to raise the bar on the learner experience and scale our impact across the central functions we serve.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in Engineering, Supply Chain, Economics or Business Administration
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience managing training/learning related projects or programs
- Experience in formulating and implementing training strategies, policies, and procedures for standardisation and delivery of training methodology throughout the organisation

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or equivalent
- Experience with instructional design, curriculum architecture, or training program development
- Experience using business metrics and training data to track, trend, and manage the impact of training efforts
- Experience with Learning Management Systems (LMS), or experience with multimedia content creation
- L&D certification by recognized body (e.g. CIPD)
- Experience in instructional design tools (e.g. Storyline, Camtasia)
- Experience with Experimental Design & Research

descriptionHtml:

- Teilnahme in übergeordneten Projekten zur Optimierung der Kundenzufriedenheit

Du arbeitest in einer unserer Schichten (Früh-, Spät- oder Nachtschicht). Dabei ist das Einhalten der Sicherheitsstandards an deinem gesamten Standort für dich höchste Priorität. Als Schichtleitung führst du routinemäßig Teammeetings durch und führst Feedbackgespräche mit deinen Mitarbeitenden und deinen Stakeholdern. Mit Hilfe von Datenauswertungen nimmst Du Einfluss auf die Produktivität und die Qualität deines Standortes. Als wichtiges Mitglied des Teams vor Ort arbeitest Du mit anderen Abteilungen, sowie externen Stakeholdern zusammen und sorgst dafür, dass wir die Anforderungen unserer Kundschaft, ebenso wie unsere eigenen Vorgaben jederzeit erfüllen. Durch die Analyse von Daten mit Führungskräften und die Besprechung der betrieblichen Vor- und Nachteile von technischen Verbesserungen mit den Fachabteilungen trägst du zu „best in class“ Lösungen bei.

About the team
Amazon Logistik (AMZL) ist für die Auslieferung von Millionen von Produkten unserer Kunden und Kundinnen direkt an die Haustür verantwortlich. Unser Ziel ist es, das Liefererlebnis für unsere Kund:innen so reibungslos wie möglich zu machen und globale Lieferlösungen für unsere neuesten Angebote einzuführen, darunter Amazon Fresh, Prime Now und Amazon Restaurants.
Unsere Arbeit lässt sich in zwei Sparten unterteilen. „Under the Roof“ betrifft alles was innerhalb unserer Logistikstandorte passiert und „On the Road“ alles was in den Liefergebieten auf der Straße stattfindet. Unsere Mitarbeitenden bereiten die Pakete in entsprechenden Schichten (Nacht, Früh, Spät) auf den täglichen Versand an unsere Lieferteams vor und kümmern sich um Retouren, die nicht ausgeliefert werden konnten.
Jedes Jahr setzen wir neue Maßstäbe in puncto Kundenerlebnis und bieten neue, innovative Lieferdienste an. Wir suchen nach neuen Möglichkeiten, um branchenweite Logistikherausforderungen zu überwinden, sowie nach neuen Ideen, um unseren CO2-Fußabdruck zu reduzieren. Ein Fuhrpark innovativer Fahrzeuge (einschließlich E-Fahrzeugen) und modernste Technologie unterstützen uns dabei.

- Relevante Erfahrung in der Durchführung von Datenanalysen

title: Principal Product Manager – Technical, Circular Economy, Extended Producer Responsbility
descriptionHtml:
Would you like to build technology products that help shape Amazon’s transition toward a more circular economy? Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations are rapidly changing how producers and retailers manage products and packaging after sale, including recycling obligations, fees, reporting, seller compliance, and reverse logistics. Amazon is building the technology and operating mechanisms required to manage these obligations at global scale while creating the foundation for broader circularity services.

As a Principal Product Manager – Technical, you will define and lead the product strategy for some of Amazon’s most complex sustainability and regulatory challenges. You will work across engineering, science, compliance, finance, operations, and sustainability teams to automate global EPR programs, improve product and packaging data, enable compliant selling partners, and develop scalable capabilities for recycling, recovery, and circularity.

This role requires a product leader who can operate in significant ambiguity, translate evolving regulatory and business requirements into durable technical solutions, and influence across a broad set of senior stakeholders. You will help determine where Amazon should build common global platforms versus localized solutions, establish mechanisms that improve accuracy and reduce manual effort, and shape new services that can support both compliance and circular-economy objectives.

This is a high-visibility opportunity to build at the intersection of technology, regulation, sustainability, and Amazon-scale commerce, with the ability to influence how Amazon manages producer responsibility today and how it develops broader circularity capabilities for the future.

Key job responsibilities
-Define and deliver AI-enabled products that scale global EPR compliance, including monitoring emerging regulations and policy changes, translating requirements into product and control strategies, and enabling rapid expansion across new geographies and regulatory use cases.
-Improve the Selling Partner compliance experience by building products that make requirements easier to understand and act on, reduce the effort and cost required to achieve compliance, and enable sellers to continue offering products across Amazon stores.
Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for EPR and circular economy, leading 3-Year Vision, annual operating planning, and quarterly prioritization while aligning investments across business, technology, compliance, sustainability, and operations teams.
-Drive automation and simplification across Amazon’s EPR operating model, replacing manual processes with scalable technology, improving data and classification accuracy, and strengthening controls across reporting, fees, registrations, and compliance monitoring.
-Develop new circular-economy capabilities and services across recycling, recovery, reverse logistics, and producer accountability, identifying opportunities where Amazon can meet regulatory requirements while improving customer and Selling Partner experiences.
-Influence and align senior cross-functional leaders across engineering, science, finance, legal, public policy, operations, and sustainability to resolve ambiguous problems, make investment tradeoffs, and deliver durable global solutions.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience in technical product management, program management or engineering
- Experience leading engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience as a strong leader who can prioritize well, communicate clearly and effectively influence across cross-functional teams

Preferred qualifications

- Experience technical product management
- Experience in project management methodologies, business analysis, or process improvement
- Experience owning data-centric products
- Experience interpreting and communicating analytics

title: Sr. Solutions Architect, Cross-Industry Greenfield
descriptionHtml:
This is the role where architecture meets impact. The Account Solutions Architect (SA) is the trusted technical advisor that customers rely on from first engagement through production and beyond - building sustained technical relationships, understanding customer objectives, and guiding them toward solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes. Through ongoing technical credibility and a commitment to the customer's success, the Account SA drives adoption and deepens engagement in ways that produce lasting business outcomes as the enduring technical voice that earns and maintains customer trust as a member of the account team.

The SA validates recommendations through hands-on building, turning architectural insight into working solutions that earn customer trust.
The Account SA provides prescriptive technical guidance - selecting services, designing secure, resilient and scalable architectures, optimizing for cost and performance, and surfacing risks early. Operates as a hands-on builder in the customer's [non-production] environment, validating solutions through working proof points (PoCs, prototypes, reference implementations) because working solutions earn trust that documents cannot. The role scales impact beyond individual engagements by contributing reusable assets other practitioners adopt, orchestrating access to deeper expertise when needed, and transferring capability so customers achieve self-sufficiency rather than dependency.

Key job responsibilities
Technical Solution Design & Customer Advisory
• Designs end-to-end solutions for customer workloads, making trade-off decisions across security, scalability, reliability, performance, cost, and operational efficiency while navigating constraints, operational maturity, and competing business priorities.
• Acts as a trusted technical advisor to the customer's technical and business stakeholders, understanding business objectives, technology landscape, and industry context to recommend fit-for-purpose solutions that connect architectural decisions to long-term business outcomes.
• Advances customer decisions across complex stakeholder groups by making business outcomes (cost reduction, time-to-value, return on investment) tangible and credible through the appropriate combination of architectural reasoning, technical proof, or working demonstrations.
• Evaluates existing customer architectures to identify gaps, risks, modernization and optimization opportunities; delivers actionable remediation guidance and modernization roadmaps.

Building & Demonstrating Solutions
• Operates as a hands-on builder who develops and validates solutions through working proof points in own sandbox and customer non-production environments - leveraging emerging technologies and AI-assisted development to accelerate proof-of-value delivery while maintaining security and operational rigor.
• Applies a production mindset from the outset, integrating governance, security, resiliency, observability, and human validation of critical deliverables into all demonstrable artifacts. Delivers solutions to Amazon Coding Bar (technical standards): tested, secure, and maintainable by others.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Partners with sales, business development, professional services, support, product/engineering teams, and external partners teams to move solutions from adoption through launch, orchestrating multi-team delivery against a shared architecture.
• Provides technical input to product teams by translating customer evidence into clear, actionable requirements that tighten the feedback loop between Account engagements and product direction.

Enablement & Organizational Development
• Improves how the team operates by driving process changes, knowledge transfer, mentoring others, leading design reviews, creating reusable assets (code, tooling, reference implementations) that scale best practices, and recruiting technical talent to sustain a high-performing team.

Thought Leadership & Content Development
• Develops and delivers prescriptive technical content - reference architectures, workshops, white papers, blog posts, and presentations - that shifts how other technical practitioners deliver and educates the broader technical community.
• Represents the organization at industry events, customer forums, and technical conferences as a recognized technical voice.


A day in the life
Your day starts with context - reviewing where your customers are in their technical journey, what's changed in their environment, and what's next. You might open with a design session where you're whiteboarding architecture options with a customer's engineering team, making trade-off decisions together, and committing to a direction. By mid-morning, you're building - writing code, deploying infrastructure, or extending a proof of concept in a sandbox to validate what you recommended yesterday.
After lunch, you're in a customer strategy session with your account team - advising on technical direction, connecting technical progress to business outcomes, navigating competing priorities, and aligning on what proof point will give the customer's decision-makers confidence to move forward. Not everything is clear-cut; you often work with incomplete information, shifting requirements, and stakeholders who don't yet agree on the problem - and you move things forward anyway.
Your week includes time you protect for keeping current - whether that's tracking emerging technologies, following industry shifts, or getting hands-on with a new service before a customer asks about it. You invest in the broader SA community too: mentoring a newer SA through a complex engagement or publishing a reference architecture from a recent win so others don't start from scratch. Travel is part of the rhythm - you're on-site with customers as the role requires, varying by geography and customer portfolio, because trust is built faster in person and the best architectural decisions happen at the whiteboard, not over email.

Diverse Experiences

Ingenuity is the main mechanism which supports our focus on quality, speed, and cost.
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to become part of a global engineering team, responsible for the design and continuous innovation of our rapidly expanding data center foot print.

Engineers at Amazon work to design resilient, cost effective mechanical distribution systems. As engineers at Amazon we are responsible for achieving a world class uptime for our customers. We justify and communicate the technical decisions we make to Sr. Management and work hard to drive continuous advancements and improvements with our designs. As an engineer at Amazon you have the ability to drive change and define/design the systems our customers rely on.

Amazon offers a fast paced, fun, and exciting work environment. title: Sr. RF and Wireless Systems Engineer, Amazon Leo Digital RF Systems
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.


The Role:
As a Sr. RF and Wireless Systems Engineer in the Digital RF Systems team, you will be responsible for RF architecture definition, RF line-up design, and RF specifications of custom ASICs used in Leo phased array systems.

You will work closely with RFIC and DSP designers during the design phase, participating in RFIC design reviews to ensure optimal system-level RF performance.

You will use MATLAB, ADS and other simulation tools to model RF impairments of the chips and analyze complex phased array system and sub-system interactions. In post-silicon, you will be involved in prototyping, defining RF DVT lab test requirements to validate designs. You will support production teams through statistical analysis and yield optimization in cross-functional collaboration with manufacturing engineers.

You will develop novel techniques to estimate and correct RF impairments such as IQ imbalance, LOFT implemented in hardware and firmware. Based on system-level constraints such as low power and cost, you will develop optimized solutions to support high throughput for our customers. You will engage with an experienced cross-disciplinary staff to conceive and design innovative product solutions, working closely with internal teams including ASIC/RFIC designers, firmware/software engineers, and design verification engineers. You will drive key aspects of wireless product design identifying ASIC level specifications from the product requirements.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.





Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end RF architecture and line-up design for the Leo RFICs and phased array communication systems used in the satellites and customer terminals
- Define RF specifications, key performance requirements for custom ASIC development
- Simulate and characterize RF impairments impact on the system
- Review RFIC designs for compliance with system performance targets
- Research and implement calibration and correction algorithms for RF front-end impairments
- Involve in lab validation plans for post-silicon RF characterization
- Identify and resolve RF performance bottlenecks through measurements and analysis
- Balance power, cost, and throughput trade-offs to meet product requirements
- Support ASIC production data reviews to drive yield improvements with manufacturing engineering
- Serve as the RF systems point of contact across silicon design, firmware, software, and test teams

Basic qualifications

- Master's degree or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering or related field
- 7+ years of relevant experience in wireless DSP/RF systems engineering (LTE, 5G-NR, WiFi 802.11, BLE)
- In depth knowledge of RF architectures and design for low power consumption RFIC and ASIC
- Solid understanding of RF blocks and components, RF simulation tools
- Experience in RF impairment estimation and compensation techniques
- Working knowledge of FW implementation of various DSP algorithms for RF impairment compensation
- Experience in using lab equipment, bring-up and validation of chip
- Experience with MATLAB, Python and/or C/C++ for fixed point DSP algorithm development, RF impairment modeling and simulation
- MSEE/PhD is highly preferred with emphasis on RF systems, mmWave RFIC designs

Preferred qualifications

- Strong background in RFIC design process
- Digital/Wireless Communication Systems and engineering
- Experience in designing low power/area digital signal processing blocks for Wireless RF SOCs
- Excellent understanding of RF architectures and blocks used in the Wireless SOCs
- MATLAB, Python, C++ experience with emphasis on fixed point modeling of DSP blocks, RF impairment modeling, RF calibration algorithm development, system performance simulations (EVM, ACLR, OOB emissions)
- Familiarity with phased array systems and phased array performance optimization techniques
- Experience in silicon bring-up in the lab and using lab equipment such as vector spectrum analyzer, signal generators, high speed scopes and logic analyzers
- Proficiency in Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS simulation tools
