title: Network Infrastructure Construction Quality Engineer, Global Network Deployment Quality Assurance Cabling
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) designs, plans, delivers, and operates all AWS global infrastructure. We keep the cloud running by supporting AWS data centers and the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that give customers continual access to innovation. We solve complex problems with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain.

You'll join software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other essential roles. You'll collaborate across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing capacity at the lowest cost for customers.

In this role, you will:

Work with construction teams to integrate quality assurance into data center network pathway infrastructure construction throughout the project lifecycle. You'll participate in construction design reviews, page turns, and reviews for construction documents, providing Quality Assurance representation to ensure standards are met during construction. You'll influence construction managers, general contractors, Colocation providers and relevant contractors to adopt quality assurance checklists that validate conformance to both Amazon and jurisdictional standards during critical construction milestone checks for pathway infrastructure.

You'll bring the voice of the customer forward by gathering feedback from construction teams and internal stakeholders to refine quality processes. You'll verify that pathway infrastructure construction meets installation requirements by reviewing documentation and data from milestone inspections. You'll document and align on construction standards and standard operating procedures as new technology and construction methods integrate into our infrastructure. You’ll also conduct training with construction managers, and provide guidelines to general contractors, Colocation providers and contractors to ensure consistent execution across all construction activities.

This role matters because construction quality directly impacts data center reliability and customer experience. You'll own the quality process from participating in construction design reviews through training delivery, ensuring our infrastructure meets the standards our customers depend on.

This is an opportunity to leverage and grow your existing program management, quality assurance and engineering experience in an innovative and highly collaborative environment where the results of your work will directly impact AWS and its customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Fluent in Spanish

- Own Quality Assurance related programs to drive world-class quality in network infrastructure in the new construction of Data Centers to achieve the best operating, lowest cost infrastructure in the world. The Network Infra Quality Engineer - Construction will be obsessed with quality, engineering, and design continuous improvements

- Review cable tray designs against Amazon’s Policies and Industry Standards and define acceptance checklists for each build milestone

- Partner with Construction Management team and Technical Infrastructure Project Manager to ensure network pathway infrastructures are built according to design documents and build project milestones, document early signals for risks and escalate to respective owners for remediations

- Capture requirement variants between approved design and physical installation and collaborate with onsite teams and design teams to close gaps in pathway infrastructure installation methods.

- Define and maintain updates of Quality Assurance documents including inspection checklists and installation requirements from design specifications, Quality Assurance standard operating procedures, Global Design Standards documents, Global Installation Best Practice Guidelines, Product Specifications for Inside Plant cable routing, and Quality Issue trackers.

- Monitor installations and collect lessons learned on network pathway quality

- Define Network Pathway Infrastructure Quality Training Programs, and the creation of training materials, to support Construction teams and as reference guidelines for vendors.

- Define quality and operational metrics related to construction performance, establish measurement frameworks, and analyze data to drive strategic improvements and inform decision-making

- Regional and Local Travel up to 25% to perform site visits and meetings for onsite quality standards review and collect feedback from onsite personnel

A day in the life
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a highly innovative company that collaborates across disciplines to produce new technology that changes our world. The AWS Quality Team is a fast-growing global team that is rethinking the implementation and design for the critical arteries that connect the various pieces of hardware inside AWS’ data centers and edge sites.

As a member of this team, you will be charged with visiting our data centers and ensuring that we are following AWS and Industry standards while also collecting lessons learned so we are continually improving. You will work directly with engineers, managers, and operations teams across the company to develop and improve network pathway and installation standards based on these observations and lessons learned.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience with power management and power monitoring systems
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Electrical, Mechanical, Structural Engineering or equivalent field
- Experience in root cause analysis and error correction, identifying changes to procedures and systems to implement long-term fixes and avoid repeating issues
- 4+ years of experience in network pathway infrastructure design or installation in data center environments
- Experience conducting quality inspections in live data center environments with engagement of contractors, engineers, and stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of engineering documentation, electrical diagrams and standard operating procedures
- Knowledge of building codes and regulations including Life Safety, BOCA, NFPA, NEC, or OSHA
- Experience in Data Center Engineering Operations, with a deep understanding of electrical and mechanical data center infrastructure
- Experience reading and interpreting construction specifications and drawings for all domains
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in managing and troublshooting network

title: Software Development Engineer, Inter Datacenter Network Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's network is one of the largest in the world, and we are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to help build the intelligent controllers that decide how traffic moves across it. In this role you will tackle optimization and distributed-systems problems at regional scale, designing and delivering software that makes our network faster, more reliable, and more efficient. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, from defining requirements through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operations. If you enjoy translating hard technical problems into clean, well-tested code and want your work to have visible, global impact, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build components of intelligent network controllers, working with senior and principal engineers to align on system architecture and tradeoffs around scalability, performance, and security.
- Write high-quality, maintainable, and well-documented code across major portions of the team's systems, ensuring it can be extended by engineers who are not yet familiar with the codebase.
- Participate actively in operational support for the controllers, identifying root causes of issues and driving permanent fixes while continuously improving the team's operational processes.
- Mentor other engineers through code reviews and design discussions, raising the overall quality bar and helping teammates grow their skills.
- Evaluate new tools, approaches, and generative artificial intelligence capabilities to improve productivity, code quality, and the algorithms that power traffic optimization.

A day in the life
You might start by reviewing a design proposal from a teammate, offering feedback that sharpens the approach before code is written. Later you could be prototyping a new optimization algorithm alongside a scientist, then writing the distributed service that puts it into production. When an operational issue surfaces, you will dig into metrics with network engineers to find the root cause and ship a permanent fix. Throughout the day you will collaborate with a cross-disciplinary group of software engineers, scientists, and network engineers who all contribute to how traffic flows across Amazon's network.

About the team
Our team builds the intelligent traffic-engineering systems that shape how data moves across Amazon's global network. We are a cross-disciplinary group of software engineers, scientists, and network engineers, and we value an inclusive culture where every perspective strengthens our solutions. Right now we are investing in the next generation of intelligent traffic engineering, and this role will be central to that effort. If you want to solve optimization and large-scale distributed-systems problems that have real, measurable impact on network performance worldwide, this is the team to join.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: IT Support Associate II, Ops Tech Solutions (OTS)
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. OpsTech IT provides nonstop global IT support to Amazon Operations as a vital piece to the puzzle. We are looking for self-motivated individuals to take on new challenges and motivate teams in fostering solutions to the hurdles we face. Together, we take ownership for what we do — whether supporting IT infrastructure, developing new technology in-house, launching a new Amazon Operations facility, or delighting our customers by delivering packages directly to them.

About The Role
As an IT Support Associate II, you will use your skills to support the operations team in resolving technical problems within Amazon operations facilities in a defined geographical area that span across a multitude of technical disciplines. We are committed to improvement; you will be encouraged to participate in career development opportunities as presented to progress your career at Amazon.

What Do We Offer?
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there’s more: we are a casual dress code at each of our locations (jeans, t-shirts, safety shoes and at times a neon safety vest will be your daily outfit). Learn more about Amazon in Andy Jassy's most recent letter to shareholders at https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/2021-letter-to-shareholders.

Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- Allocating, maintaining, and troubleshooting of IT equipment used in Amazon Operations facilities.
- Handling support requests and procedures across the network.
- Assisting in training new hires.
- Continuous learning of new technologies.
- Supporting customers from multiple buildings in the area, as well as remote customers.
- Moving up to 49lbs as well as standing and walking for shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
- Traveling within your local or regional area to support our customers.

descriptionHtml:

As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.



A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings

title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, Digital Messaging, Amazon Connect
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Amazon Connect is an AI-powered customer experience solution that enables superior outcomes at a lower cost. Since its 2017 public launch, Amazon Connect has become an AI leader, transforming how organizations of all types interact with their customers.

Amazon Connect Customer, within AWS is a highly disruptive AWS product. Digital Messaging team owns the front door for all agentic and non-agentic conversations, delivering best-in-class customer experience for variety of personas.

We're looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer (SDE III ) to help shape the next generation of guided visual experiences for millions of Amazon Connect customers worldwide. This is a high-ownership role on a team where your technical decisions will directly influence how agentic customer experience design, build, deploy, and deliver guided workflows to brand agents and their customers.

You will design and build systems that span multiple rendering surfaces (Agent workspace, Agentic Canvas, Messaging platforms, Brands self-service portals), multiple consumers (human builders, AI agents, 1P application teams), and multiple modalities (visual, conversational, text-based). The problems are real and nuanced — runtime performance at global scale, cross-channel fidelity, component composability, and deeply interleaved lifecycles between Guides, Chat, and Flows.

The Guides & Views team within Amazon Connect Customer's Digital Messaging Engine org, owns the *guided visual experience layer* — the system that powers dynamic, interactive interfaces for agents, customers, and AI-driven workflows across Amazon Connect. When someone sees a step-by-step guided workflow, a custom dashboard, or a rich interactive message on WhatsApp, Apple Messages, SMS, or web chat inside Connect, it's built on our platform.

We are a team of engineers solving problems at the intersection of *no-code UI tooling*, *real-time workflow orchestration*, *cross-channel rendering*, and *AI-composed experiences*. Our products include:

- *Guides* — guided, branching workflows that walk agents through complex business processes during live contacts
- *Views* — a dynamic UI framework that lets contact center managers design and deploy rich visual experiences without writing code
- *Interactive Messaging* — a unified representation for rich messages across all of Connect's chat channels (Web Chat, WhatsApp, Apple Messages for Business, SMS)
- *AI-composed experiences* — the visual building blocks consumed and composed by AI agents at runtime as part of the Agentic Canvas initiative

We're building the interface that hundreds of thousands of contact center agents use every day, and we're evolving it from a human-authored tool into a platform that AI agents can compose in real time.

Key job responsibilities
- Own and drive technical design for complex, ambiguous problems across the Guides & Views stack — from the no-code UI Builder to the runtime rendering engine to cross-channel interactive messaging
- Architect platform capabilities that serve both our own Guides product and a growing set of internal consumers (Agentic Canvas, Cases, Customer Profiles, Chat/Messaging, Q in Connect)
- Lead the evolution of Views from a single-surface renderer to a multi-surface, multi-channel platform that renders consistently across agent workspace, conversational AI interfaces, messaging platforms, mobile, and web
- Design and implement AI integration points that enable AI agents to compose, pre-populate, and orchestrate guided visual experiences at runtime
- Raise the technical bar through code reviews, design reviews, operational excellence, and mentoring of junior and mid-level engineers
- Influence the roadmap by identifying technical investments that unlock customer value and reduce long-term operational burden
- Own operational health, participate in on-call rotations, drive down operational load, and build systems that are observable, resilient, and self-healing

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

descriptionHtml:

Our entire business works hard to delight our customers – from the second an order is placed online to the seamless coordination of that order behind the scenes, we strive to stay agile, fluid and intentional. That can be described in one of our core Leadership Principles, which is Bias for Action. This means that our teams band together, roll up their sleeves, and aren’t content with just standing still. We’re aiming to become the most customer-centric company on Earth.

Rural Super Rural (RSR) is an exciting organization within Amazon dedicated to ensuring our customers receive their deliveries and are satisfied with their service, even in our most remote area. We are a combination of operations and support teams aligned to continually strive to innovate the last mile delivery process while bringing smiles to our customer’s faces.

title: Data Science Manager, Security Compliance Engineering, Stores Security
descriptionHtml:
Security is moving from something builders stop for to something that runs quietly inside how they already work: guidance that shows up in their tools as they code, and continuous checks that replace the weeks-long review queue. Behind that shift is data. Knowing which controls a service actually needs, surfacing where real risk lives across a massive portfolio, whether the guidance we give is accurate enough to trust, and whether any of it is genuinely reducing risk. You'll lead the data science and data engineering team that answers those questions and makes that whole model measurable.

Proving efficacy at scale is where you'll have the biggest impact. It's easy to ship guidance, but hard to know it's working: that it's accurate, that builders act on it, that fewer issues reach production because of it. You'll own the data that turns those into answers leaders can act on, and the feedback loop that uses every issue we find to make the guidance smarter so the same problem never recurs.

You'll be the leader who gets the craft of data scientists, data engineers, and business intelligence engineers, and can bring them together as one group with a shared direction. You'll set the vision, raise the technical bar, and build the foundations good science depends on: trusted data, reliable pipelines, and reproducible research.

You'll love this role if you enjoy:

- Turning security from a gate into a default, and proving with data that the shift actually works.
- Finding where risk really lives, using data and models to surface the issues and high-risk code that matter most before they reach production.
- Answering hard measurement questions at scale: is our guidance accurate, are builders acting on it, are fewer issues reaching production?
- Working across disciplines, using science, analytics, and engineering together so each makes the others stronger.
- Standing up something new: shaping the strategy, culture, and standards for a team ready for its first dedicated data leader.
- Growing engineers and scientists and watching them take on bigger scope because of how you invested in them.

Key job responsibilities
- Set the strategy, roadmap, and technical direction for a combined data science and data engineering team, turning an ambiguous, fast-moving security mission into clear, prioritized work and partnering with tech and business leadership to shape the vision.
- Own how we measure whether embedded security is working: build the metrics, experiments, and analysis that show whether guidance is accurate, whether builders act on it, and whether fewer issues reach production because of it.
- Lead the data science behind risk identification and the compounding feedback loop: surface where real risk lives across a large portfolio, scope which controls each service needs, and make sure every issue found feeds back into smarter guidance so the same problem does not recur.
- Determine the right mix of science, data engineering, and BI resources, use those disciplines to complement rather than duplicate one another, and lead senior individual contributors credibly across both the science and engineering sides of the team.
- Hold the bar on quality and delivery: judge whether outputs are trustworthy and ready to inform decisions or ship, without letting work be under-scoped or over-engineered, and invest in the data foundation of trusted data, reliable pipelines, and reproducible research. Own the results and credit the people who deliver them.
- Grow the team and manage ambiguity: develop scientists and engineers into bigger scope, support in-flight discipline transitions, establish the shared standards and data culture that let the team deliver without you, and mitigate risks and escalate with good judgment before they become roadblocks.

title: Payroll Manager - CZE
descriptionHtml:
Want to own payroll end to end for a whole country, and shape how it is done rather than just keep it running? This is your chance to lead payroll for Amazon employees in Czech Republic and make a real difference to their experience.
You lead a payroll team and are the single point of contact for your scope. Working to a defined strategy, you set team structure and priorities, improve how the work is done, and own compliance and controllership readiness. You will innovate — moving away from manual, traditional ways of working — handle Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs), country expansions and mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and build an environment where people develop and do their best work. This role is part of the EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa) Payroll Management Team.
A typical week: you set priorities and team structure, review service levels and quality, make operational decisions using data, anticipate what employees need from payroll, negotiate priorities with partner teams and payroll vendors, and develop your team.


Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• Own the end-to-end payroll cycle for Czech Republic and act as the single point of contact for your scope
• Lead and develop your payroll team, setting team structure and priorities
• Improve payroll processes and the employee payroll experience, reducing the effort for employees to access payroll services
• Own compliance and controllership readiness, including Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls; run Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs)
• Lead country expansions and mergers and acquisitions (M&A); manage payroll vendors and works councils where applicable

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing key financial metrics and preparing for a working session with your team on an upcoming business review. After coaching a team member through a complex variance analysis, you join a cross-functional meeting to align on resource priorities for the quarter. In the afternoon, you review a financial package your team prepared, provide detailed feedback, and wrap up by discussing career development goals during a one-on-one with a direct report.

title: Software Development Engineer II
descriptionHtml:
Are you looking for an opportunity to build a highly available, large scale, enterprise-wide software solution? Does it excite you to find patterns and build generic, composable software solutions to solve complex problems? Are you looking for inventing newer and simpler ways of building solutions? If so, we are looking for you to fill a challenging position in Amazon Finance Automation Payroll Technology team.
Payroll Technology at Amazon is all about enabling our business to perform at scale as efficiently as possible with no defects. As Amazon's workforce grows, both in size and geography, Amazon's payroll operations become increasingly complex, and our customers are asked to do more with less. Process can only get them so far, and that's where we come in with technology solutions to integrate and automate systems, detect defects before payment, and provide insights.  As an SDE II on our team, you will be responsible for leading the architecture, design, development and launch of some of the core product features. You will have significant influence on our overall strategy by helping define these product features, drive the system architecture, and spearhead the best practices to delivery high quality products.
This position requires that you are a significant and autonomous contributor. Your work is consistently high quality. You solve complex problems, applying appropriate technologies and best practices. Your focus is on designing, developing and effectively applying automated solutions that test major portions of software (e.g., significant component, set of features, mid-size application, service, etc.). You prevent and find defects early. You apply software testing techniques, such as equivalence class partitioning, boundary value testing, etc. You build complete test and/or measurement solutions (e.g., performance, load, scalability, usability, etc.) You use data from testing, deployment, and production to measure quality and provide actionable improvement to the product. You write code that an SDE unfamiliar with the system can understand. You are proficient in a broad range of design approaches and know when it is appropriate to make trade-offs. Your solutions are pragmatic. You do things with the proper level of complexity the first time (or at least minimize incidental complexity). You consider the legacy of the code you produce, limiting the use of short-term workarounds. You create flexible software without over-engineering. You re-use where possible, while being judicious about introducing dependencies. You are efficient with resource usage (e.g., designing to avoid impacting the system under test.)
This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned engineer. In this position, you will play a leading role in the architecture, design, implementation and deployment of large-scale and complex financial applications. You will push your design and architecture limits by inventing and simplifying complex problems. You have strong verbal and written communication skills, are self-driven, and can deliver high quality results in a fast-paced environment. You will work with Amazon engineering and business teams across the globe in planning, designing, executing and implementing this new platform.

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

title: Senior Financial Analyst, Alexa Finance, Alexa Finance
descriptionHtml:
Drive the Financial Strategy Behind One of Amazon's Most Transformative Businesses

Amazon's Alexa organization is redefining how hundreds of millions of customers interact with technology — and we need a Senior Financial Analyst on our Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team who wants to be at the center of it. This isn't a back-office finance role. You'll sit at the intersection of strategy and execution — owning the financial planning, forecasting, and analytical frameworks that guide how Alexa invests, grows, and scales. From building the models that shape OP cycles to delivering variance analyses that change the conversation in leadership reviews, your work will have direct, measurable impact on one of the fastest-growing businesses in Amazon's portfolio.

What You'll Do
Own the Planning Cycle End-to-End — Lead the financial planning and forecasting processes (OP1, OP2, monthly/quarterly guidance) for your business area, building high-fidelity models that translate strategic ambitions into actionable financial plans with robust checks and balances.

Deliver Actionable Variance & Performance Analysis — Go beyond reporting the numbers. Conduct deep-dive variance analyses (actuals vs. plan, month-over-month, year-over-year), identify the why behind the trends, and surface insights that drive corrective action and inform forward-looking decisions.

Partner as a Strategic Finance Advisor — Work directly with business leaders and senior executives as a trusted thought partner — not just a number provider. Translate financial data into strategic narratives that influence investment priorities, resource allocation, and long-range planning.

Build & Maintain Scalable Financial Models — Design and own sophisticated P&L, revenue, and cost models that support scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and business case development. Your models will be the foundation for decisions worth millions.

Drive Cross-Functional Alignment — Collaborate with product, engineering, marketing, and operations teams to ensure financial perspectives are embedded in business decisions. Own the bridge between operational metrics and financial outcomes.

Elevate the FP&A Function — Identify opportunities to automate, streamline, and improve existing planning and reporting processes. Bring a continuous improvement mindset to how the team operates — think mechanisms, not just deliverables.

What Makes This Role Special
Strategic Seat at the Table — FP&A at Alexa isn't a support function; it's a strategic partner. You'll have regular visibility with VPs and Directors, and your analyses will directly shape how the business allocates capital and prioritizes investments.
Impact at Scale — Alexa touches hundreds of millions of customers worldwide. The financial frameworks you build will influence how Amazon invests in AI, voice technology, and the next generation of ambient computing.

Intellectual Depth — This is a business that thrives in ambiguity. You'll tackle complex, undefined problems — from emerging revenue streams to evolving cost structures — where the right financial lens can unlock entirely new ways of thinking.

Growth Trajectory — The Alexa business is evolving rapidly, creating abundant opportunities for expanded scope, increased ownership, and career acceleration within Amazon Finance.

What We're Looking For
A self-starter who thrives in ambiguity and sees undefined problems as opportunities, not obstacles

Strong FP&A fundamentals — you're fluent in planning cycles, P&L management, variance analysis, and financial modeling
Exceptional Excel/financial modeling skills with a keen attention to detail and a commitment to high-fidelity outputs

Proven ability to manage multiple high-priority workstreams simultaneously (OP cycles, monthly closes, ad-hoc analyses) without sacrificing quality
Strong interpersonal and communication skills — you can distill complex financial narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences, and you're comfortable presenting to senior leadership

Experience building scalable processes and mechanisms, not just one-off analyses
Intellectual curiosity and a genuine passion for understanding what drives business performance at a unit-economic level

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of applying key financial performance indicators (KPIs) to analyses experience
- 3+ years of creating process improvements with automation and analysis experience
- 3+ years of identifying, leading, and executing opportunities to improve, automate, standardize or simplify finance or business tools and processes experience
- 3+ years of finance, accounting, or related analytical field experience
- Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, tax, economics, or a related analytical field
- 3+ years of dissecting financial data and identifying patterns that support business strategy experience
- 3+ years of contributing to cross-functional initiatives that drive financial performance and strategy experience

Preferred qualifications

- 4+ years of participating in continuous improvement projects in your team to scale and improve controllership with measurable results experience
- MBA, or CPA
- Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (examples: SQL, MS Access, Essbase, Cognos) and other financial systems (examples: Oracle, SAP, Lawson, JD Edwards)

Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. title: Software Development Engineer II, CloudWatch Collectors
descriptionHtml:
Come and build the future with us as we change the way the world sees the Cloud!

CloudWatch is the observability platform of AWS, built for developers, system operators, site reliability engineers (SRE), and IT managers. CloudWatch collects monitoring and operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events, providing a unified view of AWS resources, applications and services that run on AWS, and on-premises servers. Customers use CloudWatch to set high resolution alarms, visualise logs and metrics side by side, take automated actions, troubleshoot issues, and discover insights to optimise their applications, and ensure they are running smoothly. The CloudWatch team in Dublin is growing and we are looking for exceptional software development engineers to create the next generation CloudWatch experience.

CloudWatch is one of the largest real time data platforms in the world, processing more than 68 quadrillion metric observations per month and growing fast! This requires teams in CloudWatch to innovate at an unprecedented scale. In CloudWatch we love giving customers what they want: high quality, highly usable, highly available services. It's humbling and energizing to work with excellent, dedicated engineers to build and deliver world-leading service monitoring solutions at AWS scale.

We're looking for a new teammate who is enthusiastic, empathetic, curious, motivated, reliable, and able to work effectively with a diverse team of peers; someone who will help us amplify the positive & inclusive team culture we've been building.

Key job responsibilities
As a Software Development Engineer for the CloudWatch organisation, you will work in an agile team to design, build and maintain highly available, massively scaled systems used by millions of users worldwide. You will design and implement complex software to the highest quality for the services you and your team own, building our telemetry collection agents in Rust and Go and engaging with the upstream open-source communities, such as OpenTelemetry, that our software is built on and contributes to.

You will help expand our services across all AWS Regions, and when issues arise you will dive deep to understand the root cause and apply fixes that prevent them recurring. You will leverage GenAI and AI-powered development tools to enhance your productivity while staying current with emerging technologies, and you will also mentor junior engineers, helping grow the technical capability of the team.

A day in the life
On a typical day you might root-cause a collection issue affecting a fleet of hosts, ship a new feature in one of our agents, take a change upstream to OpenTelemetry, or design a solution to a performance or footprint problem you have never seen before. You translate customer and internal requirements into designs, weigh the tradeoffs, and break the work into incremental deliverables your team can ship. A strong community of senior and principal engineers gives direct feedback and pushes your thinking. You are surrounded by people who are passionate about observability and who believe there is still a lot of ground to cover in helping developers, SREs, and operators understand their systems.

About the team
We own telemetry collection for CloudWatch: the agents that run on millions of hosts and containers across AWS and gather the metrics, logs, and traces that everything else in CloudWatch is built on. Our software is written in Rust and Go and built on OpenTelemetry, and we contribute back to those open-source communities. We are a growing team in Dublin, and our mission is to give every AWS customer a reliable, low-overhead way to collect the telemetry their systems produce.

We invest in growing our engineers from day one. You will be paired with a buddy, work closely with senior and principal engineers.

Basic qualifications

- Experience (non-internship) in professional software development
- Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
- Hands on programming skills in at least one of the following: Rust, Go, Java, C++, Python

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Experience with full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations
- Open-source enthusiasm and contributions (e.g. a GitHub portfolio, or contributions to projects such as OpenTelemetry)

title: Applied Science Manager, Seller Partner Trust and Store Integrity Science - Global Risk Intelligence and Prevention
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an Applied Science Manager III to lead a team of applied scientists building next-generation AI-powered seller risk detection systems. This role sits at the intersection of deep technical science, strategic planning, and cross-organizational partnership. GRIP Science serves a complex stakeholder landscape: enforcement teams, policy owners, marketplace operations, peer science orgs, and senior leadership, each with distinct timelines and priorities. The right leader for this role will navigate that landscape with clarity, balancing urgent operational needs against the long-term scientific investments required to stay ahead of adversarial actors at scale.

You will independently own the vision, roadmap, and execution for a critical detection surface, defining what to build, what to defer, and how to measure success. You will set and maintain a high bar for scientific rigor while cultivating a team culture that rewards creative problem-solving and principled risk-taking.

Key job responsibilities
Strategy & Stakeholder Partnership

• Define the scientific vision and multi-year roadmap for your team's detection domain, ensuring alignment across a broad set of stakeholders with competing priorities and timelines
• Develop strong working relationships with enforcement, policy, operations, and engineering partners; serve as the trusted scientific voice in cross-functional discussions
• Exercise judgment in sequencing work. Distinguish between high-urgency requests that warrant immediate response and those better addressed through systematic, durable solutions
• Influence org-level planning (OP1/OP2) through compelling written narratives and data-driven proposals that articulate both near-term deliverables and long-term scientific bets
• Proactively communicate trade-offs to leadership and stakeholders, building trust through transparency about what your team will and will not prioritize in a given cycle

Science & Technical Leadership

• Lead a team building state-of-the-art detection models that leverage modern AI techniques, including deep learning, foundation models, and generative AI, to identify novel abuse patterns at scale
• Set and uphold a high standard for scientific methodology: model validation, experimentation rigor, reproducibility, and interpretability of results
• Evaluate end-to-end scientific proposals for soundness, scalability, and production readiness; know when to push for deeper investigation and when to ship
• Foster a culture of scientific curiosity and invention. Encourage the team to challenge assumptions, explore out of the box approaches, and invest in research that creates step-function improvements rather than incremental gains
• Identify where emerging AI capabilities (e.g., large language models, multimodal reasoning, self-supervised learning) can be applied to unlock new detection signals or fundamentally reshape existing pipelines
• Make informed trade-offs between model sophistication, delivery timelines, and operational sustainability

Execution & Operational Excellence

• Scope scientific projects, set priorities, and drive schedules; readjust decisively when incoming signals warrant a change in direction
• Structure work to reduce exposure to classic failure modes: ambiguous requirements, untested assumptions, under-instrumented models
• Establish mechanisms and metrics to continuously measure model effectiveness, enforcement precision, and downstream business outcomes
• Drive production readiness: monitoring, alerting, on-call practices, and rapid response for AI/ML systems processing millions of daily decisions

Team Building & Development

• Build and lead a high-performing team of applied scientists; attract and develop talent that combines technical depth with ownership mindset
• Invest in the growth of individual scientists through deliberate project assignment, regular coaching, and actionable feedback tied to career progression
• Create an environment where scientists have the space to do deep work, the support to take calculated risks, and the recognition when they deliver
• Manage performance across the full spectrum. Accelerate top performers toward promotion readiness while addressing gaps constructively and with clear expectations


About the team
GRIP Science (Global Risk Intelligence & Prevention) is the core detection engine within TSI Science. We build and operate state-of-the-art ML and AI models that identify and block bad sellers across Amazon's 24 global marketplaces. Our systems cover the full seller journey, from registration through every action on the marketplace, and score holistic risk across all active sellers. We push the frontier of adversarial detection by combining large-scale deep learning, graph-based reasoning, generative AI, and real-time inference to outpace bad actors who continuously evolve their tactics. This is one of the most technically demanding and high-impact applied science problem spaces at Amazon. Your models directly shape marketplace integrity for hundreds of millions of customers worldwide.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of scientists or machine learning engineers management experience
- Knowledge of ML, NLP, Information Retrieval and Analytics
- Ph.D. in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields, or PhD and 5+ years of a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, business analytics, economics, finance, engineering, or computer science experience
- 1+ years of scientists or machine learning engineers management experience
- Experience hiring and leading experienced scientists as well as having a successful record of developing junior members from academia or industry to a successful career track
- Experience working and communicating with multiple stakeholders, C-level executives and cross-functional teams
- Experience with large scale machine learning systems such as profiling and debugging and understanding of system performance and scalability
- Experience in written and verbal communication skills to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- Experience building machine learning models or developing algorithms for business application
- Experience building complex software systems, especially involving deep learning, machine learning and computer vision, that have been successfully delivered to customers

title: System Development Engineer II, Manipulation Robotics
descriptionHtml:
Our team is pushing the limits in contact-rich manipulation for robotic systems that pick and move diverse items from cluttered containers at high speed and quality. The field has not settled which architectures, learning and controls stacks, and hardware embodiments will best solve the problem, so we need to create prototype systems quickly, test them in realistic and repeatable conditions, and adapt as we learn. We are looking for a Systems Development Engineer to develop a laboratory test strategy, design and build test infrastructure, and drive the test and learning loop. This role is hands-on, in the lab and in code.

The Manipulation Robotics team develops robotic workcells to pick, grasp, and move millions of items and packages across Amazon's fulfillment network. You will build early surrogate systems, leveraging commercial robots, off-the-shelf hardware, and open-source software where they fit, to enable testing and evaluation before the target platform is ready. As the design matures, you will collaborate closely with the controls engineers and compliant mechanism designers on the test strategy, evaluation, and iteration. Your automation and data pipelines will make results repeatable and trustworthy, giving us the evidence to support deployment and scaling decisions.

Key job responsibilities
- Build the laboratory and test infrastructure that lets the team put new grasping ideas in front of real items quickly, adapting it as the design evolves and keeping it available, maintainable, and documented so engineers and scientists can run evaluations independently.
- Bring up robot arms and workcells in the lab, including motion, safety, and integration with the test harness.
- Partner with mechanical, electrical, controls, and science engineers to answer open design questions through testing, so tradeoffs across performance, cost, complexity, and reliability get settled with data.
- Establish the characterization procedures and infrastructure that inform finger, gripper, arm, and workcell decisions, and produce the data simulation is calibrated against.
- Instrument lab setups broadly from the start, anticipating what data will be needed to answer future questions, compare architectures, and inform which sensing the production design carries.
- Own the software that makes testing possible, including hardware integration, data acquisition, test automation, and analysis tooling.
- Write and adapt bench-level controls firmware, purpose-built to get a mechanism moving and instrumented quickly so an idea can be judged while it is still cheap to change.
- Automate item presentation to support volume and repeatability testing across a variety of workflows and robot embodiments.
- Diagnose problems across hardware, software, and the operating environment when a test result and reality disagree, and eliminate the contributing cause with a permanent fix.

A day in the life
You will start your day reviewing system health dashboards and operational metrics, then shift into building or refining automation that keeps your team's services running smoothly. You might spend part of the afternoon pairing with a teammate on a design review or troubleshooting a tricky production issue. Along the way, you will collaborate with partner teams to align on technical decisions and share best practices. Expect to balance hands-on engineering with mentoring newer team members and contributing to planning discussions.

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience
- 2+ years building prototype or test hardware for electromechanical or robotic systems, including hands-on fabrication, assembly, and integrating sensors and actuators.
- Experience writing and maintaining software for hardware integration, test automation, data acquisition, or analysis, in Python, C/C++, or a related language.

title: Senior Mechatronics & Robotics Technician
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

About the Role:

As a Senior Mechatronics & Robotics Technician, you will lead service technicians in the installation and repair of automated packaging and distribution equipment. You will support the Operations Maintenance team by designing solutions for difficult problems and managing projects. You will help train and mentor service technicians and contract technicians.

What Do We Offer?
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there is more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- You will maintain and oversee material handling equipment (MHE) and facility equipment, such as Fire Life Safety (FLS) systems
- You will lead a team of service technicians and develop training plans, as well as oversee vendors making planned and emergency repairs
- You will install, maintain, and troubleshoot relay logic, ladder diagrams, control components, photo-eyes, motor starters, limit switches, proximity sensors, solenoids, etc.
- You will create and close out work orders with data including labor hours, equipment maintenance, and parts used, as well as develop job plans for emergency repair of critical assets-
- You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head
Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- 4+ years of conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures experience
- 4+ years of repairing material handling equipment (MHE), automated conveyor systems, or related mechanical/controls equipment experience
- 4+ years of reading blueprints and electrical schematics experience
- 4+ years of electrical and electronic principles experience
- 4+ years of demonstrating safety standards experience
- 4+ years of troubleshooting and diagnostics of material handling equipment (MHE) experience

Preferred qualifications

- Associate's degree in Mechatronics or a related technical field

title: Propulsion Functional Technician, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. The Propulsion team is seeking a Manufacturing Functional Technician to join the team to support production manufacturing of future flight hardware.
The Propulsion Manufacturing Functional Technician will work within the Amazon Leo Propulsion Manufacturing Team supporting the build and integration of electric propulsion subsystems, including feed systems, thrusters, cathodes, PCBAs, tanks, and the integrated propulsion system.
This technician will be knowledgeable across multiple manufacturing process paths, perform troubleshooting activities, support training programs, and lead process improvement initiatives within their scope. The ideal candidate brings hands-on manufacturing experience with flight hardware and thrives in a fast-paced production environment.

Additional Requirements:

Standing for long periods of time, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, and stretching may be required to perform the functions of this position

Able to lift-up to 25lbs. unassisted

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Candidates must be 18 years or older with the ability to understand and adhere to all job requirements and safety guidelines.

The starting pay for this role in Washington State is up to $33.50 / hour and employees are eligible for incremental raises based on tenure. This information is provided per the Washington State Pay Transparency Act. Base pay information is based on market location. Applicants should apply via Amazon’s internal or external careers site.


Key job responsibilities
Assemble, fabricate, and process materials into complex manufactured products across propulsion subsystems per engineering documentation and SOPs, following one or more defined process paths.

Learn to perform troubleshooting activities associated with manufacturing products, observing, receiving, and obtaining information from all relevant sources to assist in debug and root cause analysis. Seek guidance when deviation from available procedures is needed.

Learn to perform hardware inspections and document discrepancies. May assist with development stage assemblies and first article builds under guidance of senior peers.

Read, interpret, and work from engineering documentation and drawings following well established processes.

Provide engineers with feedback on tooling, consumables, debug observations, and process issues through structured channels such as MES WOT entries.

Identify training needs for the team and assist in the training of new hires and junior peers to help them scale in their role.

Contribute to process improvement ideas within your project scope, working with leaders and engineers individually or in group settings.

Follow best practices as defined by leaders, lead techs, manuals, and SOPs. Meet productivity and quality standards consistently.

Uphold job and site safety standards and operations protocol. Follow proper procedure when quality or safety issues occur.

Attempt to resolve individual work blockers before escalating. Identify additional tasks once assigned work is complete and communicate to Lead Technician before proceeding.

Utilize MES and SAP systems for production tracking, traceability, and work order documentation. Capture and record data accurately in applicable systems.

May assist with servicing, repairing, calibrating, regulating, fine tuning, and testing machines, devices, and equipment.

Attend all relevant technical trainings offered by the organization.

The Propulsion Manufacturing Functional Technician will perform a variety of hardware manufacturing, testing and integration tasks across propulsion subsystems to ensure hardware meets production requirements for flight. They will work closely with engineering teams to provide feedback on processes and identify improvements.
This technician is expected to be knowledgeable across multiple process paths, support peers and new hires, and lead process improvements within their scope. They will utilize MES and SAP systems for daily production tracking and traceability and will actively support the team in resolving work blockers and general operational needs.
A successful candidate thrives in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment and can apply their technical expertise and commitment to quality to positively impact team metrics and organization goals. To be successful they will need to be highly motivated and detail oriented while showing the highest standards of execution.

About the team
The Amazon Leo Propulsion Team is responsible for the design and development of the propulsion system which provides maneuvering capability to the spacecraft. The Propulsion Team is made up of a variety of sub-teams which are responsible for various aspects of the development process, such as mechanical design, systems engineering, subject matter experts, manufacturing, and test. This integrated team structure allows direct communication and rapid process feedback while also promoting close collaboration across the team.

- 2+ year’s experience in a fast-paced production environment with flight hardware
- 2+ years of hands-on experience with precision torque, measurement and inspection devices (i.e., automated and manual torque wrenches, calipers, micrometers, profilometers, optical inspection devices, multi-meters, etc.)

descriptionHtml:
A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDEs write production-grade software and own outcomes end-to-end, from prototype through enterprise-scale deployment combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes. They create reusable architectures, patterns, and engineering mechanisms that scale the entire FDE practice.

Key job responsibilities
Lead technical delivery across customer engagements
- Own the technical strategy and execution for complex, multi-workstream customer AI programs. Make architecture decisions that span multiple services and organizational boundaries. Align technical approach with the customer's long-term technology strategy. Requires 30–50% travel.

Architect and build production AI systems at scale
- Design the foundational architectures — multi-agent orchestration, enterprise retrieval systems, decision intelligence platforms — for the most complex customer engagements. Drive clarity where neither the business problem nor technology approach is fully defined. Build production systems that handle enterprise-scale traffic and reliability requirements.

Own production excellence across workstreams
- Define operational standards, evaluation frameworks, and production readiness criteria for AI systems across your engagement scope. Establish mechanisms (testing strategies, observability standards, incident response playbooks) that ensure AI systems remain healthy. Drive operational improvements that raise the bar for the team.

Scale the team's effectiveness
- Define engineering patterns, contribute to the interview and hiring process, and mentor junior FDEs into independent contributors. Coach others on system design, customer engagement, and production operations. Drive engineering excellence standards within your scope.

Accelerate customer transformation
- Identify systemic opportunities to expand AI adoption across the customer organization. Create accelerators and reusable platforms that reduce time-to-value from months to weeks. Feed learnings back into AWS services and the FDE practice.

title: Sr. TPM – Antenna Dev, Amazon Leo Antenna Development
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager for Antenna Calibration, you will own the end-to-end program management of antenna calibration system development, from requirements definition through design, integration, and test. You will define and manage the interfaces between hardware and software subsystems, drive alignment across engineering teams on requirements and technical approach, and organize cross-functional efforts to deliver calibration solutions on schedule. This role carries direct responsibility for system-level program and project management, including ownership of the calibration test strategy and design trade-off decisions. In this role, your responsibilities will include:
- Own the program roadmap and execution plan for antenna calibration system development, including defining milestones, managing dependencies, and driving delivery across multiple engineering teams

- Drive the calibration test strategy, including test architecture, measurement methodology, and pass/fail criteria, in partnership with RF and systems engineering teams

- Identify and manage technical risks and trade-offs, escalating decisions to leadership with clear data and recommendations
- Establish and maintain software release processes, including CI/CD pipeline management, build and deployment schedules, version control practices, and cross-team coordination mechanisms

title: Program Manager, Amazon Automated Reasoning
descriptionHtml:
The Automated Reasoning team seeks a Program Manager to drive critical initiatives supporting Amazon's Automated Reasoning (AR) community, focusing on building connections between internal teams across Amazon, external academic partnerships, and educational programs. This role requires working closely with AR scientists and leaders while navigating Amazon's culture and business requirements to drive meaningful impact for the AR community.

As a field, automated reasoning answers questions about the future behavior of computer systems: what they might do, what they will do, or what they can never do. Because these tools use mathematical logic, they are capable of providing accurate reasoning about intractably large or possibly unbounded systems, e.g. network behaviors, policy semantics, program state-spaces.

- Manage conference and summer school sponsorships from end to end: intake, communication, benefit management, and payment logistics.

The Automated Reasoning PM team serves as the backbone for Amazon's critical AR initiatives, which power essential Amazon services in Identity, Agent AR, Security, and many more! title: Support Engineer I - Ext, Partner Tech Engineering
descriptionHtml:

The Partner Tech organization builds innovative software solutions and owns the customer experience for Advertisers and Partners integrating with our API and MCP. Our products are strategically important to Amazon's Retail and Marketplace businesses, driving long-term growth. We deliver billions of ad impressions and millions of clicks daily and are breaking fresh ground to create world-class products. We are a highly motivated, collaborative organization with an entrepreneurial spirit and bias for action. With a broad mandate to experiment and innovate, we are growing at an unprecedented scale with a seemingly endless range of new opportunities.



Are you passionate about driving customer success and learning new technologies? Do you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment? Amazon Advertising is seeking Support Engineers to help external customers build business-critical applications on our Advertising API. You will represent Amazon as you investigate technical issues, work with API developers to ensure compliance with our program policies and identify gaps in our technical solutions as well as patterns of API misuse. You will own development of processes and prevention strategies to improve the developer experience. Working directly with Advertising API engineers and the onboarding team, you will ensure customer issues are resolved quickly and effectively.

Key job responsibilities
Support Engineers troubleshoot, debug, evaluate, and resolve system-generated alerts, make feature enhancements and bug fixes, manage systems and hosts, perform software deployments and migrations, and automate routine operational tasks. The position requires strong troubleshooting, technical, and communication skills, and includes a mix of on-call responsibilities, operational tasks, and software development work. You will develop tools and automation to drive toward human-free operations.

This role is ideal if you are passionate about creating, integrating, and leveraging tools to minimize operational overhead — without compromising best-in-class customer service. We want our services to be as autonomous as possible, and that requires engineers who think big, simplify complex problems, and relentlessly pursue the best customer experience. Our environment is built for engineers who flourish in building automation to reduce operational workload rather than simply performing operational tasks.

Successful candidates will join an elite Advertising API support team, provide troubleshooting and operations support, and innovate to replace manual tasks with scripts and code.

A day in the life
Provide solutions to product and API-related questions raised through partner engagements

Identify key product architecture components, and propose and build solutions that unblock partner integrations

Write code samples, tutorials, and technical articles for the developer community

Audit partner behavior to ensure compliance with program policies

Work with customers to understand how they use our services, and provide feedback to development teams to improve the onboarding experience

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to drive timely customer communication during critical events

Drive projects that improve support-related processes and the overall developer support experience

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of software development, or 1+ years of technical support experience
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
- Experience working with REST API based services
- Experience working with databases and SQL

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Knowledge of web services, distributed systems, and web application development
- Knowledge of AWS or cloud technologies
- Experience in English-language communication skills, both written and verbal

title: System Development Engineer, Battery Test Systems, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Batteries power that mission, and understanding how they perform, age, and fail depends on data. We are looking for a Systems Development Engineer to own the lab computing, networking, and data infrastructure that turns raw battery test data into fast, reliable, trustworthy insight for a growing battery team.

In this role you will own the systems that capture, move, and organize test data: keep networked test and lab PCs (Windows and Linux) patched and secure, and build, automate, and harden the pipelines that move data from local PCs to network storage to the cloud (AWS S3). You will normalize data from many tester types into a common schema, drive down manual data handling, and make the whole system more reliable, observable, and easy to operate. You will start by stabilizing and extending what exists, then take the systems in the directions that add the most value: bad-data detection and tagging, richer metadata and traceability, Grafana dashboards and metrics, and automation that removes toil.

Beyond the core infrastructure, you will build new capabilities on top of that data, including deploying and operating AI and machine-learning models over the databases to create new features for the team and our customers: turning large, messy datasets into predictions, summaries, and natural-language tools that let an engineer get to an answer quickly. As the lab and test fleet grow, you will specify the software, networking, and security requirements for new test systems and partner with vendors and internal security teams to bring them online reliably and compliantly. There is real room to broaden scope over time based on your strengths and the team's needs.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
Administer and patch networked test-floor and lab PCs (Windows and Linux) to meet evolving security requirements; automate configuration and keep systems current.
Build, automate, operate, and harden data pipelines that move test data from local test PCs to network storage to the cloud (AWS S3), with reliability and observability as first-class goals.
Maintain and extend data-homogenization code that normalizes test data from multiple tester types and formats into a common schema for shared tooling.
Improve detection, cleaning, tagging, and labeling of bad or incomplete data; incorporate metadata into the database for traceability across test types.
Build and operate summary-metric scripts, Grafana dashboards, and monitoring/alerting for production and test data systems.
Deploy and operate AI and machine-learning models on top of the databases to create new features for the team and customers, such as predictive insights, automated data-quality checks, and natural-language querying and visualization.
Build and extend implementation-level tools and small applications that make test data easier for engineers to reach and use.
Specify software, networking, and security requirements for new test equipment, and partner with vendors and internal security teams to bring new systems online reliably and compliantly.
Diagnose and resolve performance, reliability, and availability issues across hardware, software, and operating environments, leaving systems better than you found them.

A day in the life
You might start the morning confirming overnight test data landed cleanly in S3 and triaging a pipeline alert, then pair with a cell test engineer to fold a new tester's output into the common schema. In the afternoon you could automate a manual data-handling step, tune a Grafana dashboard and its alerts, prototype a model that flags suspect data before it reaches the database, and scope the network and security requirements for a tester arriving next month. The mix shifts with the team's priorities, and you decide where your time creates the most leverage.

About the team
We are the battery team behind Amazon Leo's power systems. We design, build, and test the cells and packs that keep satellites running, and we rely on a fast-growing body of test data to understand how they perform. This role owns the computing, networking, and data backbone the whole team depends on, and works closely with cell test, build, and design engineers to keep the systems reliable and remove the barriers between people and answers.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent work experience
- Experience in systems administration (Linux/Windows)
- Experience with automation or working with scripting languages like Python, Java, Perl, PHP, Ruby, Bash, Shell, or equivalent
- Experience including, building and maintaining data flows and pipelines
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with AWS Services including EC2, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, SQS
- Experience in hands-on infrastructure, troubleshooting, systems administration, networking, DevOps or applications development
- Experience deploying and operating AI or machine-learning models in production, or integrating them into data or user-facing applications (e.g., prediction, anomaly detection, or natural-language querying).
- Experience with Grafana or other monitoring, BI, and visualization tools.
- Experience with networked PC administration and patching in a lab or industrial setting.
- Experience working with manufacturing test equipment and tester data.
